pali: yadā kho te, bhikkhave, cha-ppāṇakā jhattā assu kilantā, atha tam eva khīlaṃ vā thambhaṃ vā upatiṭṭheyyuṃ, upanisīdeyyuṃ, upanipajjeyyuṃ.
en: Now when these six animals become worn out and fatigued, they would stand close to that post or pillar, they would sit down there, they would lie down there.

pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhuno kāya-gatā-sati bhāvitā bahulī-katā, taṃ cakkhu n’āviñchati manāpiyesu rūpesu, amanāpiyā rūpā na-ppaṭikūlā honti … pe … mano n’āviñchati manāpiyesu dhammesu, amanāpiyā dhammā na-ppaṭikūlā honti. evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, saṃvaro hoti.
en: So too, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu has developed and cultivated awareness directed to the body, the eye does not pull in the direction of agreeable forms nor are disagreeable forms repulsive … the mind does not pull in the direction of agreeable mental phenomena nor are disagreeable mental phenomena repulsive. It is in such a way that there is restraint.

pali: ‘daḷhe khīle vā thambhe vā’ti kho, bhikkhave, kāya-gatāya satiyā etaṃ adhivacanaṃ. tasmātiha vo, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ: ‘kāya-gatā no sati bhāvitā bhavissati bahulī-katā, yānī-katā, vatthu-katā, anuṭṭhitā, paricitā, susamāraddhā’ti. evañ hi kho, bhikkhave, sikkhitabban”ti.
en: ‘A strong post or pillar’: this, bhikkhus, is a designation for awareness directed to the body. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will develop and cultivate awareness directed to the body, make it our vehicle, make it our basis, stabilize it, exercise ourselves in it, and fully undertake it.’ Thus should you train yourselves.”

pali: “bhūta-pubbaṃ, bhikkhave, kummo kacchapo sāyanha-samayaṃ anu-nadī-tīre gocara-pasuto ahosi. siṅgālo’pi kho, bhikkhave, sāyanha-samayaṃ anu-nadī-tīre gocara-pasuto ahosi.
en: “Bhikkhus, in the past a tortoise was searching for food along the bank of a river one evening. On that same evening a jackal was also searching for food along the bank of that same river.

pali: addasā kho, bhikkhave, kummo kacchapo siṅgālaṃ dūrato’va gocara-pasutaṃ. disvāna soṇḍi-pañcamāni aṅgāni sake kapāle samodahitvā, app’ossukko tuṇhī-bhūto saṅkasāyati.
en: When the tortoise saw the jackal in the distance searching for food, it drew its limbs and neck inside its shell and passed the time keeping still and silent.

pali: siṅgālo’pi kho, bhikkhave, addasa kummaṃ kacchapaṃ dūrato’va gocara-pasutaṃ. disvāna yena kummo kacchapo ten’upasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā kummaṃ kacchapaṃ paccupaṭṭhito ahosi: ‘yad’āyaṃ kummo kacchapo soṇḍi-pañcamānaṃ aṅgānaṃ aññataraṃ vā aññataraṃ vā aṅgaṃ abhininnāmessati, tatth’eva naṃ gahetvā, uddālitvā khādissāmī’ti.
en: The jackal had also seen the tortoise in the distance searching for food, so he approached and waited close by, thinking, ‘When this tortoise extends one or another of its limbs or its neck, I will grab it right on the spot, pull it out, and eat it.’

pali: yadā kho, bhikkhave, kummo kacchapo soṇḍi-pañcamānaṃ aṅgānaṃ aññataraṃ vā aññataraṃ vā aṅgaṃ na abhininnāmi, atha siṅgālo kummamhā nibbijja pakkāmi, otāraṃ alabhamāno.
en: But because the tortoise did not extend any of its limbs or its neck, the jackal, failing to gain access to it, lost interest in it and departed.

pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, tumhe’pi māro pāpimā satataṃ samitaṃ paccupaṭṭhito: ‘app’eva nām’āhaṃ imesaṃ cakkhuto vā otāraṃ labheyyaṃ … pe … manato vā otāraṃ labheyyan’ti. tasmātiha, bhikkhave, indriyesu gutta-dvārā viharatha.
en: So too, bhikkhus, Māra the Evil One is constantly and continually waiting close by you, thinking, ‘Perhaps I will gain access to him through the eye … or through the mind.’ Therefore, bhikkhus, dwell guarding the doors of the sense faculties.

pali: cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā mā nimitta-ggāhino ahuvattha, mā anubyañjana-ggāhino. yatv’ādhikaraṇam enaṃ cakkhu’ndriyaṃ asaṃvutaṃ viharantaṃ abhijjhā-domanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṃ, tassa saṃvarāya paṭipajjatha, rakkhatha cakkhu’ndriyaṃ, cakkhu’ndriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjatha.
en: Having seen a form with the eye, do not grasp its signs and features. Since, if you leave the eye faculty unguarded, bad unwholesome states of craving and aversion might invade you, practice the way of its restraint, guard the eye faculty, undertake the restraint of the eye faculty.

pali: sotena saddaṃ sutvā … ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā … jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā … kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā … manasā dhammaṃ viññāya mā nimitta-ggāhino ahuvattha, mā anubyañjana-ggāhino … pe … man’indriye saṃvaraṃ āpajjatha.
en: Having heard a sound with the ear … Having smelled an odor with the nose … Having savoured a taste with the tongue … Having felt a tactile object with the body … Having cognized a mental phenomenon with the mind, do not grasp its signs and features … undertake the restraint of the mind faculty.

pali: yato tumhe, bhikkhave, indriyesu gutta-dvārā viharissatha, atha tumhehi’pi māro pāpimā nibbijja pakkamissati, otāraṃ alabhamāno, kummamhā’va siṅgālo”ti.
en: When, bhikkhus, you dwell guarding the doors of the sense faculties, Māra the Evil One, failing to gain access to you, will lose interest in you and depart, just as the jackal departed from the tortoise.”
Drawing in the mind’s thoughts
as a tortoise draws its limbs into its shell,
independent, not harassing others, fully quenched,
a bhikkhu would not blame anyone.

pali: taṃ suṇātha. kiñ ca, bhikkhave, sabbaṃ?
en: At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the all.
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the all?

pali: cakkhuñ c’eva rūpā ca, sotañ ca saddā ca,
ghānañ ca gandhā ca, jivhā ca rasā ca,
kāyo ca phoṭṭhabbā ca, mano ca dhammā ca.
en: The eye and visual forms, the ear and sounds,
the nose and odors, the tongue and tastes,
the body and sensations, the mind and mental objects.
This is called the all.

pali: yo, bhikkhave, evaṃ vadeyya: ‘aham etaṃ sabbaṃ paccakkhāya, aññaṃ sabbaṃ paññāpessāmī’ti.
en: If anyone, bhikkhus, should speak thus:
‘Having rejected this all, I shall make known another all.’

pali: tassa vācā’vatthurev’assa, puṭṭho ca na sampāyeyya,
en: This would be just a baseless statement on his part,
and if questioned, he would not be able to reply.
And further, he would meet with frustration. For what reason? Because, bhikkhus, that is outside his range.”

pali: ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā gayāyaṃ viharati gayā-sīse,
en: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Gayā, at Gayā’s Head, together with a thousand bhikkhus. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus: “Bhikkhus, all is burning.
And what, bhikkhus, is the all that is burning?
The eye is burning, visual forms are burning,
eye-consciousness is burning,
eye-contact is burning,

pali: yam’p’idaṃ cakkhu-samphassa-paccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā, dukkhaṃ vā, adukkham-asukhaṃ vā,
en: and whatever is felt with eye-contact as condition — whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that too is burning.

pali: jātiyā, jarāya, maraṇena, sokehi, paridevehi, dukkhehi, domanassehi, upāyāsehi ādittan’ti vadāmi.
en: Burning with what? Burning with the fire of craving, with the fire of aversion, with the fire of delusion; burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and misery, I say.

pali: sotaṃ ādittaṃ … pe … ghānaṃ ādittaṃ … pe …
jivhā ādittā … pe … kāyo āditto … pe …
en: The ear is burning … The nose is burning …
The tongue is burning … The body is burning …

pali: mano āditto, dhammā ādittā, mano-viññāṇaṃ ādittaṃ,
yam’p’idaṃ mano-samphassa-paccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā, dukkhaṃ vā,
en: The mind is burning, mental objects are burning, mind-consciousness is burning,
mind-contact is burning, and whatever is felt with mind-contact as condition —
whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that too is burning.

pali: jātiyā, jarāya, maraṇena, sokehi, paridevehi, dukkhehi, domanassehi, upāyāsehi ādittan’ti vadāmi.
en: Burning with what? Burning with the fire of craving, with the fire of aversion, with the fire of delusion; burning with birth, aging, and death; with sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and misery, I say.

pali: cakkhu-viññāṇe’pi nibbindati, cakkhu-samphasse’pi nibbindati, yam’p’idaṃ cakkhu-samphassa-paccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā, dukkhaṃ vā, adukkham-asukhaṃ vā,
en: Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple experiences disenchantment towards the eye, towards visual forms, towards eye-consciousness, towards eye-contact, towards whatever is felt with eye-contact as condition — whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant; …

pali: yam’p’idaṃ mano-samphassa-paccayā uppajjati vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā, dukkhaṃ vā, adukkham-asukhaṃ vā,
en: towards the mind … towards whatever is felt with mind-contact as condition — whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant;
Experiencing disenchantment, he becomes free from attachment. Through the fading of attachment,
he is liberated. When he is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘liberated.’
He understands: ‘Birth is finished with, the spiritual life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”

pali: idam avoca bhagavā. attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinanduṃ. imasmiñ ca pana veyyākaraṇasmiṃ bhaññamāne tassa bhikkhu-sahassassa anupādāya āsavehi cittāni vimucciṃsū”ti.
en: This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement. And while this discourse was being spoken, the minds of the thousand bhikkhus were liberated from the āsavas by non-clinging.”
“… Therefore, Bāhiya, you should train yourself thus:
‘In the seen there will be merely the seen;
in the heard there will be merely the heard;
in the sensed there will be merely the sensed;
in the cognized there will be merely the cognized.’
Thus, Bāhiya, should you train yourself.

pali: yato kho te, bāhiya, diṭṭhe diṭṭha-mattaṃ bhavissati,
en: When, Bāhiya, [regarding things seen, heard, sensed,
and cognized by you,] in the seen there will be merely the seen, in the heard there will be merely the heard,
in the sensed there will be merely the sensed,
in the cognized there will be merely the cognized,

pali: tato tvaṃ, bāhiya, nev’idha, na huraṃ,
en: then, Bāhiya, you will not be ‘with that.’
When, Bāhiya, you are not ‘with that,’
then you will not be ‘in that.’
When, Bāhiya, you are not ‘in that,’
then you will be neither here nor beyond nor in between
the two. Just this is the end of dukkha.”
Then, due to this brief Dhamma teaching of the Blessed One, Bāhiya’s mind was liberated from the āsavas by non-clinging right there and then.

SECTIONS.title: vedanā & samudayasacca
SECTIONS.sub: The Nearest Cause for the Origination of dukkha

en: Sorrow is born from craving,
from craving fear is born.
For one who is liberated from craving,
there is no sorrow; how then fear?
Wisdom is born from meditation;
without meditation wisdom withers away.
Having known these two paths
of progress and decline,
one should conduct oneself
so that wisdom develops.
The gift of Dhamma surpasses all gifts;
the taste of Dhamma surpasses all tastes;
the delight in Dhamma surpasses all delights;
the end of craving surpasses all dukkha.
The good give up [attachment to] everything.
The virtuous do not prattle desiring sensual pleasures.
When touched by pleasure or pain,
the wise show no elation or depression.
“Bhikkhus, it is for one who feels that I proclaim:
‘This is dukkha,’
I proclaim: ‘This is the origin of dukkha,’
I proclaim: ‘This is the cessation of dukkha,’
I proclaim: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of dukkha.’”

suttas.title: dukkhasamudayaṃ ariyasaccaṃ
suttas.en: The Noble Truth of the Origin of dukkha

en: “Now this, bhikkhus, is the noble truth of the origin of dukkha: it is this craving which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust,
seeking delight here and there; that is,
craving for sensual pleasures, craving for becoming, craving for non-becoming.”
(Mahākoṭṭhika:)
“It is said, ‘Feeling, feeling,’ friend.
In what sense is it called ‘feeling’?”

pali: kiñ ca vedeti? sukham’pi vedeti, dukkham’pi vedeti, adukkham-asukham’pi vedeti.
en: (Sāriputta:)
“‘It feels, it feels,’ friend; that is why ‘feeling’ is said. What does it feel? It feels pleasure, it feels pain,
it feels neither-pain-nor-pleasure.
‘It feels, it feels,’ friend, that is why ‘feeling’ is said.”

pali: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkham-asukhā vedanā. imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso vedanā”ti.
en: “Bhikkhus, there are these three vedanā. What three? Pleasant vedanā, painful vedanā, neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā. These are the three vedanā.
A disciple of the Buddha, aware,
concentrated, clearly comprehending,
understands vedanā,
and the origin of vedanā,
where they finally cease,
and the path leading to their destruction.
With the destruction of vedanā
a bhikkhu is hungerless and fully quenched.”

pali: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkham-asukhā vedanā. imā kho, bhikkhave, tisso vedanā”ti.
en: “Bhikkhus, there are these three vedanā. What three? Pleasant vedanā, painful vedanā, neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā. These are the three vedanā.
Whether it be pleasant or painful
along with the neither-painful-nor-pleasant,
both the internal and the external,
whatever there is that is felt:
having known, “This is dukkha,
deceptive, disintegrating,”
having touched and touched them, seeing their fall,
thus one loses one’s attachment for them.”

pali: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkham-asukhā vedanā.
sukhāya, bhikkhave, vedanāya rāg’ānusayo pahātabbo, dukkhāya vedanāya paṭigh’ānusayo pahātabbo,
en: “Bhikkhus, there are these three vedanā …
The latent tendency to craving should be abandoned in regard to pleasant vedanā.
The latent tendency to aversion should be abandoned in regard to painful vedanā. The latent tendency to ignorance should be abandoned in regard to
neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā.
When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has abandoned the latent tendency to craving in regard to pleasant vedanā,
the latent tendency to aversion in regard to painful vedanā,
and the latent tendency to ignorance in regard to
neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā,
then he is called a bhikkhu without latent tendencies,
one who sees rightly. He has cut off craving,
severed the fetters, and by completely breaking through conceit, he has made an end to dukkha.
When one experiences pleasure,
if one does not understand vedanā,
the tendency to craving is present
for one not seeing the way out of it.
When one experiences pain,
if one does not understand vedanā,
the tendency to aversion is present
for one not seeing the way out of it.
The One of Broad Wisdom has taught
with reference to that peaceful vedanā,
neither-painful-nor-pleasant:
if one seeks delight even in this,
one is still not liberated from dukkha.
But when a bhikkhu who is ardent
does not neglect clear comprehension,
then that wise one fully understands
vedanā in their entirety.
Having fully understood vedanā,
he is free from āsavas in this very life.
established in Dhamma, with the body’s breakup
the knowledge-master cannot be described.”

pali: “pubb’eva me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhi-sattass’eva sato etad ahosi:
en: “Bhikkhus, before my enlightenment,
while I was still a bodhisatta, not yet fully enlightened,
it occurred to me:
‘What now is vedanā?
What is the origin of vedanā?
What is the way leading to the origination of vedanā?
What is the cessation of vedanā?
What is the way leading to the cessation of vedanā?
What is the gratification in vedanā?
What is the danger?
What is the way out?’

pali: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkham-asukhā vedanā.
en: Then, bhikkhus, it occurred to me:
‘There are these three vedanā: pleasant vedanā,
painful vedanā, neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā.
This is called vedanā.
With the arising of contact there is the arising of vedanā. Craving is the way leading to the origination of vedanā. With the cessation of contact there is the cessation of vedanā.

pali: ayameva ariyo aṭṭh’aṅgiko maggo vedanā-nirodha-gāminī paṭipadā, seyyath’idaṃ:
en: This Noble Eightfold Path is the way leading to the cessation of vedanā; that is,
right view, right intention,
right speech, right action, right livelihood,
right effort, right awareness, right concentration.

pali: yaṃ vedanaṃ paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ,
en: The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on vedanā: this is the gratification in vedanā.
That vedanā is impermanent, dukkha,
and subject to change: this is the danger in vedanā.
The removal and abandonment of desire and craving
for vedanā: this is the way out of vedanā.’”

pali: sukham’pi vedanaṃ vedayati, dukkham’pi vedanaṃ vedayati, adukkham-asukham’pi vedanaṃ vedayati.
en: “Bhikkhus, the uninstructed ordinary person feels
a pleasant vedanā, a painful vedanā,
and a neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā.

pali: sukham’pi vedanaṃ vedayati, dukkham’pi vedanaṃ vedayati, adukkham-asukham’pi vedanaṃ vedayati.
en: The instructed noble disciple too feels
a pleasant vedanā, a painful vedanā,
and a neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā.

pali: tatra, bhikkhave, ko viseso, ko adhippayāso,
en: Therein, bhikkhus, what is the distinction,
the disparity, the difference between the instructed noble disciple and the uninstructed ordinary person?”

pali: sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṃyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho.
en: “Venerable sir, our Dhamma is rooted in the
Blessed One, guided by the Blessed One,
and has the Blessed One as its refuge.
It would be good if the Blessed One would clear up the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from him, the bhikkhus will remember it.”

pali: “evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. bhagavā etad avoca:
en: “Then listen and attend closely, bhikkhus,
I will speak.”
“Yes, venerable sir,” the bhikkhus replied.
The Blessed One said this:

pali: so dve vedanā vedayati — kāyikañ ca, cetasikañ ca.
en: “Bhikkhus, when the uninstructed ordinary person
is being contacted by a painful vedanā,
he sorrows, grieves, and laments;
he weeps beating his breast and becomes bewildered.
He feels two vedanā — a bodily one and a mental one.

pali: tam enaṃ dutiyena sallena anuvedhaṃ vijjheyya.
evañ hi so, bhikkhave, puriso dvi-sallena vedanaṃ vedayati.
en: Suppose someone were to strike a man with a dart,
and then strike him immediately afterwards with a second dart, so that the man would feel a vedanā caused by two darts.

pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, assutavā puthu-jjano dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno socati, kilamati, paridevati;
so dve vedanā vedayati — kāyikañ ca, cetasikañ ca.
en: So too, when the uninstructed ordinary person is being contacted by a painful vedanā, he sorrows, grieves,
and laments… he feels two vedanā —
a bodily one and a mental one.

pali: tassāyeva kho pana dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno paṭighavā hoti.
yo dukkhāya vedanāya paṭigh’ānusayo, so anuseti.
en: Being contacted by that same painful vedanā,
he harbors aversion towards it.
When he harbors aversion towards painful vedanā,
the latent tendency to aversion towards
painful vedanā lies behind this.
Being contacted by painful vedanā,
he seeks delight in sensual pleasure. For what reason?

pali: na hi so, bhikkhave, pajānāti assutavā puthu-jjano aññatra kāma-sukhā dukkhāya vedanāya nissaraṇaṃ.
yo sukhāya vedanāya rāg’ānusayo, so anuseti.
en: Because the uninstructed ordinary person does not know of a way out of painful vedanā other than sensual pleasure. When he seeks delight in sensual pleasure,
the latent tendency to craving for pleasant vedanā
lies behind this.

pali: so tāsaṃ vedanānaṃ samudayañ ca, atthaṅgamañ ca, assādañ ca, ādīnavañ ca, nissaraṇañ ca,
en: He does not understand as it really is the origin and
the passing away, the gratification, the danger,
and the way out in the case of these vedanā.

pali: atthaṅgamañ ca, assādañ ca, ādīnavañ ca,
yo adukkham-asukhāya vedanāya avijjā’nusayo, so anuseti.
en: When he does not understand these things,
the latent tendency to ignorance in regard to
neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā lies behind this.

pali: so sukhañ ce vedanaṃ vedayati, saññutto naṃ vedayati. dukkhañ ce vedanaṃ vedayati, saññutto naṃ vedayati. adukkham-asukhañ ce vedanaṃ vedayati,
en: If he feels a pleasant vedanā, he feels it attached.
If he feels a painful vedanā, he feels it attached.
If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā,
he feels it attached.

pali: ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘assutavā puthu-jjano saññutto jātiyā, jarāya, maraṇena, sokehi, paridevehi, dukkhehi, domanassehi, upāyāsehi; saññutto dukkhasmā’ti vadāmi.
en: This, bhikkhus, is called an uninstructed ordinary person who is attached to birth, aging, and death;
who is attached to sorrow, lamentation, pain,
dejection, and misery; who is attached to dukkha, I say.

pali: sutavā ca kho, bhikkhave, ariya-sāvako dukkhāya
vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno na socati, na kilamati,
na paridevati; na ura-ttāḷiṃ kandati, na sammohaṃ āpajjati.
so ekaṃ vedanaṃ vedayati — kāyikaṃ, na cetasikaṃ.
en: Bhikkhus, when the instructed noble disciple is contacted by a painful vedanā, he does not sorrow, grieve, or lament; he does not weep beating his breast and become bewildered.
He feels one vedanā — a bodily one, not a mental one.

pali: tam enaṃ dutiyena sallena anuvedhaṃ na vijjheyya.
evañ hi so, bhikkhave, puriso eka-sallena vedanaṃ vedayati.
en: Suppose someone were to strike a man with a dart,
but not strike him immediately afterwards with
a second dart, so that the man would feel
a vedanā caused by one dart only.

pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, sutavā ariya-sāvako dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno na socati,
na ura-ttāḷiṃ kandati, na sammohaṃ āpajjati.
en: So too, when the instructed noble disciple is contacted by a painful vedanā he does not sorrow,
grieve, or lament; he does not weep beating his breast and become bewildered.

pali: so ekaṃ vedanaṃ vedayati — kāyikaṃ, na cetasikaṃ. tassāyeva kho pana dukkhāya vedanāya phuṭṭho samāno paṭighavā na hoti.
en: He feels one vedanā — a bodily one, not a mental one.
Being contacted by that same painful vedanā,
he harbors no aversion towards it.

pali: yo dukkhāya vedanāya paṭigh’ānusayo, so n’ānuseti.
en: Since he harbors no aversion towards painful vedanā, the latent tendency to aversion towards painful vedanā does not lie behind this.

pali: pajānāti hi so, bhikkhave, sutavā ariya-sāvako aññatra
en: Being contacted by painful vedanā, he does not seek delight in sensual pleasure. For what reason?
Because the instructed noble disciple knows of a way out from painful vedanā other than sensual pleasure.

pali: tassa kāma-sukhaṃ n’ābhinandato, yo sukhāya vedanāya rāg’ānusayo, so n’ānuseti.
so tāsaṃ vedanānaṃ samudayañ ca, atthaṅgamañ ca, assādañ ca, ādīnavañ ca, nissaraṇañ ca,
en: Since he does not seek delight in sensual pleasure,
the latent tendency to craving for pleasant vedanā
does not lie behind this.
He understands as it really is the origin
and the passing away, the gratification, the danger,
and the way out in the case of these vedanā.

pali: tassa tāsaṃ vedanānaṃ samudayañ ca, atthaṅgamañ ca, assādañ ca, ādīnavañ ca, nissaraṇañ ca, yathā-bhūtaṃ pajānato, yo adukkham-asukhāya vedanāya avijjā’nusayo,
en: Since he understands these things, the latent tendency to ignorance in regard to neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā does not lie behind this.

pali: so sukhañ ce vedanaṃ vedayati, visaññutto naṃ vedayati. dukkhañ ce vedanaṃ vedayati, visaññutto naṃ vedayati. adukkham-asukhañ ce vedanaṃ vedayati,
en: If he feels a pleasant vedanā, he feels it unattached.
If he feels a painful vedanā, he feels it unattached.
If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā,
he feels it unattached.

pali: ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ‘sutavā ariya-sāvako visaññutto jātiyā, jarāya, maraṇena, sokehi, paridevehi,
en: This, bhikkhus, is called a noble disciple who is unattached to birth, aging, and death; who is unattached to sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection,
and misery; who is unattached to dukkha, I say.

pali: ayaṃ kho, bhikkhave, viseso, ayaṃ adhippayāso,
en: This, bhikkhus, is the distinction, the disparity,
the difference between the instructed noble disciple
and the uninstructed ordinary person.”

pali: “seyyathā’pi, bhikkhave, ākāse vividhā vātā vāyanti: puratthimā’pi vātā vāyanti, pacchimā’pi vātā vāyanti,
uttarā’pi vātā vāyanti, dakkhiṇā’pi vātā vāyanti,
sarajā’pi vātā vāyanti, arajā’pi vātā vāyanti,
sītā’pi vātā vāyanti, uṇhā’pi vātā vāyanti,
parittā’pi vātā vāyanti, adhimattā’pi vātā vāyanti.
en: “Bhikkhus, just as various winds blow in the sky:
winds from the east, winds from the west,
winds from the north, winds from the south,
dusty winds and dustless winds,
cold winds and hot winds,
mild winds and strong winds;
so too, various vedanā arise in this body:
pleasant vedanā arises,
painful vedanā arises,
neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā arises.
Just as many diverse winds
blow back and forth across the sky:
easterly winds and westerly winds,
northerly winds and southerly winds,
dusty winds and dustless winds,
sometimes cold, sometimes hot,
those that are strong and others mild —
winds of many kinds that blow;
so too in this very body
various kinds of vedanā arise,
pleasant ones and painful ones,
and those neither painful nor pleasant.
But when a bhikkhu who is ardent
does not neglect clear comprehension,
then that wise one fully understands
vedanā in their entirety.
Having fully understood vedanā,
he is free from āsavas in this very life.
Established in Dhamma, with the body’s breakup
the knowledge-master cannot be described.”

pali: udake udaka-bubbuḷaṃ uppajjati c’eva nirujjhati ca.
en: “Suppose, bhikkhus, that in the autumn, when it is raining and large raindrops are falling, a water bubble forms and bursts on the surface of the water.

pali: tam enaṃ cakkhumā puriso passeyya, nijjhāyeyya,
yoniso upaparikkheyya. tassa taṃ passato, nijjhāyato,
en: A man with good sight would observe it,
examine it, and carefully investigate it.
In doing so, it would appear to him as hollow,
empty, substanceless.

pali: kiñ hi siyā, bhikkhave, udaka-bubbuḷe sāro?
evameva kho, bhikkhave, yā kāci vedanā
oḷārikā vā sukhumā vā, hīnā vā paṇītā vā,
en: For what substance could there be in a water bubble?
So too, bhikkhus, whatever kind of vedanā there is,
whether past, future, or present,
internal or external, gross or subtle,
inferior or superior, far or near:

pali: taṃ bhikkhu passati, nijjhāyati, yoniso upaparikkhati.
tassa taṃ passato, nijjhāyato, yoniso upaparikkhato rittakaññeva khāyati, tucchakaññeva khāyati,
kiñ hi siyā, bhikkhave, vedanāya sāro?”
en: a bhikkhu observes it, examines it,
and carefully investigates it.
In doing so, it appears to him as hollow,
empty, substanceless.
For what substance could there be in vedanā?”

pali: atha kho sakko devānam-indo yena bhagavā ten’upasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā, bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā, ekam antaṃ aṭṭhāsi. ekam antaṃ ṭhito kho sakko devānam-indo bhagavantaṃ etad avoca:
en: Then Sakka, ruler of gods, went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, he stood at one side and asked:

pali: “kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhu saṃkhittena taṇhā-saṅkhaya-vimutto hoti, accanta-niṭṭho, accanta-yoga-kkhemī, accanta-brahma-cārī, accanta-pariyosāno, seṭṭho deva-manussānan”ti?
en: “Venerable sir, how in brief is a bhikkhu liberated in the destruction of craving, one who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate security from bondage, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal, one who is foremost among gods and humans?”

pali: “idha, devānam-inda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti: ‘sabbe dhammā n’ālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. evañ c’etaṃ, devānam-inda, bhikkhuno sutaṃ hoti: ‘sabbe dhammā n’ālaṃ abhinivesāyā’ti. so sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhijānāti; sabbaṃ dhammaṃ abhiññāya, sabbaṃ dhammaṃ parijānāti;
en: “Here, ruler of gods, a bhikkhu has heard that nothing is worth adhering to. When a bhikkhu has heard that nothing is worth adhering to, he directly knows everything; having directly known everything, he fully understands everything;

pali: sabbaṃ dhammaṃ pariññāya, yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti — sukhaṃ vā, dukkhaṃ vā, adukkham-asukhaṃ vā — so tāsu vedanāsu anicc’ānupassī viharati, virāg’ānupassī viharati, nirodh’ānupassī viharati, paṭinissagg’ānupassī viharati.
en: having fully understood everything, whatever vedanā he feels, whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant, he abides observing impermanence in those vedanā, observing fading away, observing cessation, observing relinquishment.

pali: so tāsu vedanāsu anicc’ānupassī viharanto, virāg’ānupassī viharanto, nirodh’ānupassī viharanto, paṭinissagg’ānupassī viharanto, na kiñci loke upādiyati. anupādiyaṃ na paritassati, aparitassaṃ paccattaññeva parinibbāyati: ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahma-cariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, n’āparaṃ itthattāyā’ti pajānāti.
en: Observing thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. When he does not cling, he is not agitated. When he is not agitated, he personally attains nibbāna. He understands: ‘Birth is destroyed, the spiritual life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more coming to any state of being.’

pali: ettāvatā kho, devānam-inda, bhikkhu saṃkhittena taṇhā-saṅkhaya-vimutto hoti, accanta-niṭṭho, accanta-yoga-kkhemī, accanta-brahma-cārī, accanta-pariyosāno, seṭṭho deva-manussānan”ti.
en: Briefly, it is in this way, ruler of gods, that a bhikkhu is liberated in the destruction of craving, one who has reached the ultimate end, the ultimate security from bondage, the ultimate spiritual life, the ultimate goal, one who is foremost among gods and humans.”
One may live a hundred years
without seeing the Deathless state.
Better it is a single day of life
for one seeing the Deathless state.
One may live a hundred years
without seeing the highest Dhamma.
Better it is a single day of life
for one seeing the highest Dhamma.
Through many births in saṃsāra
have I wandered in vain,
searching for the builder of the house;
birth again and again is dukkha.
O house-builder, you are seen!
You will not build a house again.
For your rafters are broken
and your ridgepole shattered.
The mind has gone into the unconditioned
and achieved the destruction of all craving.

pali: yo dhammaṃ passati, so paṭicca-samuppādaṃ passatī’”ti.
en: (Sāriputta:)
“Now this has been said by the Blessed One:
‘One who sees dependent origination sees Dhamma;
one who sees Dhamma sees dependent origination.’”
“Therein, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple attends closely and carefully to dependent origination itself thus:

pali: ‘iti imasmiṃ sati, idaṃ hoti, imass’uppādā, idaṃ uppajjati;
imasmiṃ asati, idaṃ na hoti, imassa nirodhā, idaṃ nirujjhatī’ti.”
en: ‘When this exists, that comes to be;
with the arising of this, that arises.
When this does not exist, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases.’”

suttas.title: kiṃvādī satthā?
suttas.en: The Teaching of the Great samaṇa

en: (Sāriputta:)
“Say little or say much,
tell me just the essence!
I am concerned only with the essence.
What to do with many words?”

pali: atha kho āyasmā assaji sāriputtassa paribbājakassa
en: Then the Venerable Assaji delivered this Dhamma exposition to the wanderer Sāriputta:
“Those things that arise from a cause,
the Tathāgata has revealed their cause,
and also their cessation.
Such is the teaching of the great samaṇa.”

pali: evaṃ me sutaṃ. ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ
en: Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus: “Bhikkhus!”—
“Venerable sir!” those bhikkhus replied.
The Blessed One said this:

pali: taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti.
“evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. bhagavā etad avoca:
en: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you dependent origination. Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.” —
“Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied.
The Blessed One said this:
“And what, bhikkhus, is dependent origination?
With ignorance as condition, saṅkhāras [come to be]; with saṅkhāras as condition, consciousness;
with consciousness as condition, mind and matter;
with mind and matter as condition, the six sense bases; with the six sense bases as condition, contact;
with contact as condition, vedanā;
with vedanā as condition, craving;
with craving as condition, clinging;
with clinging as condition, becoming;
with becoming as condition, birth;

pali: evam etassa kevalassa dukkha-kkhandhassa samudayo hoti.
en: with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and misery come to be. Such is the origin of this whole mass of dukkha.
This, bhikkhus, is called dependent origination.

pali: avijjāya tveva asesa-virāga-nirodhā saṅkhāra-nirodho; saṅkhāra-nirodhā viññāṇa-nirodho;
en: But with the remainderless fading away
and cessation of ignorance comes cessation
of saṅkhāras; with the cessation of saṅkhāras,
cessation of consciousness;
with the cessation of consciousness, cessation of mind and matter; with the cessation of mind and matter, cessation of the six sense bases; with the cessation
of the six sense bases, cessation of contact;

with the cessation of contact, cessation of vedanā; with the cessation of vedanā, cessation of craving; with the cessation of craving, cessation of clinging; with the cessation of clinging, cessation of becoming; with the cessation of becoming, cessation of birth;

pali: evam etassa kevalassa dukkha-kkhandhassa nirodho hotī”ti.
en: with the cessation of birth, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and misery cease.
Such is the cessation of this whole mass of dukkha.”

pali: attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandun”ti.
en: This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.”

suttas.title: dukkhanirodhaṃ ariyasaccaṃ
suttas.en: The Noble Truth of the Cessation of dukkha

en: “Now this, bhikkhus, is the noble truth of the cessation of dukkha: it is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving, the giving up and relinquishing of it, freedom from it, letting go of it.
This is called the noble truth of the cessation of dukkha.”

pali: “… so cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā piya-rūpe rūpe na sārajjati, appiya-rūpe rūpe na byāpajjati,
en: “… On seeing a visual form with the eye, he is not infatuated with it if it is pleasing; he is not repelled by it if it is unpleasing. He abides with awareness of the body established, with an unlimited mind,

pali: tañ ca ceto-vimuttiṃ paññā-vimuttiṃ yathā-bhūtaṃ pajānāti, yatth’assa te pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
en: and he understands as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein those bad unwholesome states cease without remainder.

pali: so evaṃ anurodha-virodha-vippahīno yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti, sukhaṃ vā, dukkhaṃ vā, adukkham-asukhaṃ vā,
en: Having thus abandoned attraction and repulsion,
whatever vedanā he feels, whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant, he does not delight in that vedanā, embrace it, or remain holding to it.

pali: tassa taṃ vedanaṃ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā vedanāsu nandī sā nirujjhati.
en: As he does not do so, delight in vedanā ceases in him.

pali: evam etassa kevalassa dukkha-kkhandhassa nirodho hoti.
en: With the cessation of delight comes cessation of clinging; with the cessation of clinging, cessation of becoming;
with the cessation of becoming, cessation of birth;
with the cessation of birth, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and misery cease.
Such is the cessation of this whole mass of dukkha.
On hearing a sound with the ear…
On smelling an odor with the nose…
On tasting a flavor with the tongue…
On experiencing a sensation with the body…

pali: na sārajjati, appiya-rūpe dhamme na byāpajjati,
yathā-bhūtaṃ pajānāti, yatth’assa te pāpakā akusalā dhammā aparisesā nirujjhanti.
en: On cognizing a mental object with the mind,
he is not infatuated with it if it is pleasing;
he is not repelled by it if it is unpleasing.
He abides with awareness of the body established,
with an unlimited mind, and he understands as it actually is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein those bad unwholesome states cease without remainder.

pali: so evaṃ anurodha-virodha-vippahīno yaṃ kiñci vedanaṃ vedeti, sukhaṃ vā, dukkhaṃ vā, adukkham-asukhaṃ vā,
n’ājjhosāya tiṭṭhati. tassa taṃ vedanaṃ anabhinandato, anabhivadato, anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato,
en: Having thus abandoned attraction and repulsion,
whatever vedanā he feels, whether pleasant or painful
or neither-painful-nor-pleasant,
he does not delight in that vedanā,
embrace it, or remain holding to it.
As he does not do so, delight in vedanā ceases in him.

pali: evam etassa kevalassa dukkha-kkhandhassa nirodho hoti.”
en: With the cessation of his delight comes cessation of clinging; with the cessation of clinging, cessation of becoming; with the cessation of becoming, cessation of birth; with the cessation of birth, aging and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, dejection, and misery cease.
Such is the cessation of this whole mass of dukkha.”
This is the victory indeed of a glorious Buddha,
and wicked Māra’s defeat.
Overjoyed at the seat of awakening,
the masses of devas then proclaimed
the victory of the great sage.

pali: kiñ ca, bhikkhave, jānato, kiṃ passato,
en: At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I say that the destruction of the āsavas is for one who knows and sees,
not for one who does not know and does not see.
For one who knows what, for one who sees what,
does the destruction of the āsavas come about?

pali: iti vedanā … pe … iti saññā … iti saṅkhārā …
iti viññāṇaṃ, iti viññāṇassa samudayo, iti viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo’ti. evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, jānato,
en: ‘Such is material form, such its origin, such its passing away; such is vedanā … such is perception … such are saṅkhāras … such is consciousness, such its origin, such its passing away’: it is for one who knows thus, for one who sees thus, that the destruction of the āsavas comes about.

pali: yam’pi’ssa taṃ, bhikkhave, khayasmiṃ khaye ñāṇaṃ,
kā ca, bhikkhave, khaye ñāṇassa upanisā?
en: I say, bhikkhus, that the knowledge of destruction in regard to destruction has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for the knowledge
of destruction?
It should be said: liberation.

pali: no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, vimuttiyā upanisā?
en: I say, bhikkhus, that liberation too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for liberation?
It should be said: dispassion.

pali: no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, virāgassa upanisā?
en: I say, bhikkhus, that dispassion too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for dispassion?
It should be said: disenchantment.
I say, bhikkhus, that disenchantment too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause. And what is the proximate cause for disenchantment? It should be said:
the knowledge and vision of things as they really are.

pali: no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, samādhissa upanisā?
no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, sukhassa upanisā? ‘passaddhī’ti’ssa vacanīyaṃ.
en: I say, bhikkhus, that the knowledge and vision of things as they really are too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause. And what is the proximate cause for the knowledge and vision of things as they really are? It should be said: concentration.
I say, bhikkhus, that concentration too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for concentration?
It should be said: pleasure.
I say, bhikkhus, that pleasure too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for pleasure?
It should be said: tranquility.

pali: no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, pītiyā upanisā?
no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, saddhāya upanisā? ‘dukkhan’ti’ssa vacanīyaṃ.
no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, dukkhassa upanisā?
no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, jātiyā upanisā?
no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, bhavassa upanisā?
en: I say, bhikkhus, that tranquility too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for tranquility?
It should be said: rapture.
I say, bhikkhus, that rapture too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for rapture?
It should be said: joy.
I say, bhikkhus, that joy too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for joy?
It should be said: devotion.
I say, bhikkhus, that devotion too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for devotion?
It should be said: dukkha.
I say, bhikkhus, that dukkha too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for dukkha?
It should be said: birth.
I say, bhikkhus, that birth too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for birth?
It should be said: becoming. I say, bhikkhus, that becoming too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause. And what is the proximate cause for becoming?
It should be said: clinging.

pali: no anupanisaṃ. kā ca, bhikkhave, upādānassa upanisā?
en: I say, bhikkhus, that clinging too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for clinging?
It should be said: craving.
I say, bhikkhus, that craving too has a proximate cause;
it does not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for craving?
It should be said: vedanā.
For vedanā, it should be said: contact.
For contact: the six sense bases.
For the six sense bases: mind and matter.
For mind and matter: consciousness.
For consciousness: saṅkhāras.
I say, bhikkhus, that saṅkhāras too have a proximate cause; they do not lack a proximate cause.
And what is the proximate cause for saṅkhāras?
It should be said: ignorance.
Thus, bhikkhus, with ignorance as proximate cause,
saṅkhāras [come to be];
with saṅkhāras as proximate cause, consciousness;
with consciousness as proximate cause, mind and matter; with mind and matter as proximate cause,
the six sense bases;
with the six sense bases as proximate cause, contact;
with contact as proximate cause, vedanā;
with vedanā as proximate cause, craving;
with craving as proximate cause, clinging;
with clinging as proximate cause, becoming;
with becoming as proximate cause, birth;
with birth as proximate cause, dukkha;
with dukkha as proximate cause, devotion;
with devotion as proximate cause, joy;
with joy as proximate cause, rapture;
with rapture as proximate cause, tranquility;
with tranquility as proximate cause, pleasure;
with pleasure as proximate cause, concentration;
with concentration as proximate cause,
the knowledge and vision of things as they really are;
with the knowledge and vision of things as they really are as proximate cause, disenchantment;
with disenchantment as proximate cause, dispassion;
with dispassion as proximate cause, liberation;
with liberation as proximate cause,
the knowledge of destruction.

pali: seyyathā’pi, bhikkhave, upari-pabbate thulla-phusitake deve vassante, taṃ udakaṃ yathā-ninnaṃ pavattamānaṃ pabbata-kandara-padara-sākhā paripūreti. pabbata-kandara-padara-sākhā-paripūrā kusobbhe paripūrenti.
en: Just as, bhikkhus, when rain pours down in thick droplets
on a mountain top, the water flows down along the slope and fills the mountain’s clefts, gullies, and creeks;
these being full fill up the pools;
these being full fill up the lakes;
these being full fill up the streams;
these being full fill up the rivers;
and these being full fill up the great ocean;

pali: evameva kho, bhikkhave, avijj’ūpanisā saṅkhārā, saṅkhār’ūpanisaṃ viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇ’ūpanisaṃ
saḷ-āyatan’ūpaniso phasso, phass’ūpanisā vedanā, vedan’ūpanisā taṇhā, taṇh’ūpanisaṃ upādānaṃ, upādān’ūpaniso bhavo, bhav’ūpanisā jāti,
jāt’ūpanisaṃ dukkhaṃ, dukkh’ūpanisā saddhā, saddh’ūpanisaṃ pāmojjaṃ, pāmojj’ūpanisā pīti,
pīt’ūpanisā passaddhi, passaddh’ūpanisaṃ sukhaṃ, sukh’ūpaniso samādhi,
en: so too, with ignorance as proximate cause,
saṅkhāras [come to be];
with saṅkhāras as proximate cause, consciousness …
with liberation as proximate cause,
the knowledge of destruction.”

pali: ‘ito pubbe avijjā n’āhosi, atha pacchā samabhavī’ti.
evañ c’etaṃ, bhikkhave, vuccati, atha ca pana paññāyati: ‘ida’ppaccayā avijjā’ti.
en: “Bhikkhus, a first point of ignorance is not discerned such that one might say: ‘Before this there was no ignorance and afterward it came into being.’
Still, ignorance is discerned to have a specific condition.
I say, bhikkhus, that ignorance has a nutriment;
it is not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for ignorance?
It should be said: the five hindrances.

pali: no anāhāre. ko c’āhāro pañcannaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ?
en: The five hindrances, too, I say, have a nutriment;
they are not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for the five hindrances?
It should be said: the three kinds of misconduct.

pali: no anāhārāni. ko c’āhāro tiṇṇaṃ duccaritānaṃ?
en: The three kinds of misconduct, too, I say, have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment.

And what is the nutriment for the three kinds of misconduct? It should be said: non-restraint of the sense faculties. Non-restraint of the sense faculties, too, I say, has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for non-restraint of the sense faculties?
It should be said: lack of awareness and
clear comprehension. Lack of awareness and
clear comprehension, too, I say, has a nutriment;
it is not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for lack of awareness and clear comprehension?
It should be said: unwise attention.
Unwise attention, too, I say, has a nutriment;
it is not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for unwise attention?
It should be said: lack of devotion.
Lack of devotion, too, I say, has a nutriment;
it is not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for lack of devotion?
It should be said: not hearing the good Dhamma.
Not hearing the good Dhamma, too, I say,
has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for not hearing the
good Dhamma? It should be said:
not associating with good persons.

pali: asat’āsampajaññaṃ paripūreti; asat’āsampajaññaṃ paripūraṃ, indriy’āsaṃvaraṃ paripūreti;
tīṇi duccaritāni paripūrāni, pañca nīvaraṇe paripūrenti;
evam etissā avijjāya āhāro hoti, evañ ca pāripūri.
en: Thus not associating with good persons, becoming full, fills up not hearing the good Dhamma.
Not hearing the good Dhamma, becoming full, fills up lack of devotion. Lack of devotion, becoming full, fills up unwise attention. Unwise attention, becoming full,
fills up lack of awareness and clear comprehension.
Lack of awareness and clear comprehension, becoming full, fills up non-restraint of the sense faculties.
Non-restraint of the sense faculties, becoming full,
fills up the three kinds of misconduct. The three kinds of misconduct, becoming full, fill up the five hindrances.
The five hindrances, becoming full, fill up ignorance. Thus there is nutriment for ignorance,
and in this way it becomes full.

pali: seyyathā’pi, bhikkhave, upari-pabbate thulla-phusitake deve vassante, taṃ udakaṃ yathā-ninnaṃ pavattamānaṃ
evam etassa mahā-samuddassa sāgarassa āhāro hoti,
en: Just as, when it is raining and the rain pours down in thick droplets on a mountaintop, the water flows down along the slope and fills the mountain’s clefts, gullies, and creeks; these, becoming full, fill up the pools;
these, becoming full, fill up the lakes;
these, becoming full, fill up the streams;
these, becoming full, fill up the rivers;
and these, becoming full, fill up the great ocean;
thus there is nutriment for the great ocean,
and in this way it becomes full.

pali: evam evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappurisa-saṃsevo paripūro, asaddhamma-ssavanaṃ paripūreti;
tīṇi duccaritāni paripūrāni, pañca nīvaraṇe paripūrenti;
evam etissā avijjāya āhāro hoti, evañ ca pāripūri.
en: So too, not associating with good persons,
becoming full, fills up not hearing the good Dhamma….
The five hindrances, becoming full, fill up ignorance. Thus there is nutriment for ignorance, and in this way it becomes full.

pali: no anāhāre. ko c’āhāro sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ?
en: I say, bhikkhus, that (1) true knowledge and liberation have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for true knowledge and liberation? It should be said: (2) the seven factors of enlightenment. The seven factors of enlightenment,
too, I say, have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the seven factors of enlightenment? It should be said:
(3) the four establishments of awareness.

pali: no anāhāre. ko c’āhāro catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ?
en: The four establishments of awareness, too, I say, have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the four establishments of awareness? It should be said: (4) the three kinds of good conduct. The three kinds of good conduct, too,

I say, have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the three kinds of good conduct? It should be said: (5) restraint of the sense faculties. Restraint of the sense faculties, too, I say, has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for restraint of the sense faculties? It should be said: (6) awareness and clear comprehension.
Awareness and clear comprehension, too, I say,
have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for awareness and
clear comprehension?
It should be said: (7) wise attention.
Wise attention, too, I say, has a nutriment;
it is not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for wise attention?
It should be said: (8) devotion. Devotion, too, I say,
has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment.
And what is the nutriment for devotion?
It should be said: (9) hearing the good Dhamma.
Hearing the good Dhamma, too, I say, has a nutriment;
it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for hearing the good Dhamma? It should be said:
(10) associating with good persons.

pali: iti kho, bhikkhave, sappurisa-saṃsevo paripūro, saddhamma-ssavanaṃ paripūreti;
tīṇi sucaritāni paripūrāni, cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti;
cattāro satipaṭṭhānā paripūrā, satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti;
evam etissā vijjā-vimuttiyā āhāro hoti, evañ ca pāripūri.
en: Thus associating with good persons, becoming full,
fills up hearing the good Dhamma. Hearing the good Dhamma, becoming full, fills up devotion.
Devotion, becoming full, fills up wise attention.

Wise attention, becoming full, fills up awareness and clear comprehension. … fill up restraint of the sense faculties. … fills up the three kinds of good conduct. … fill up the four establishments of awareness. …
fill up the seven factors of enlightenment.
The seven factors of enlightenment, becoming full,
fill up true knowledge and liberation.
Thus there is nutriment for true knowledge and liberation, and in this way they become full.

pali: seyyathā’pi, bhikkhave, upari-pabbate thulla-phusitake deve vassante, taṃ udakaṃ yathā-ninnaṃ pavattamānaṃ
pabbata-kandara-padara-sākhā-paripūrā kusobbhe paripūrenti; kusobbhā paripūrā mahā-sobbhe paripūrenti;
evam etassa mahā-samuddassa sāgarassa āhāro hoti,
en: Just as, when it is raining and the rain pours down in thick droplets on a mountaintop, the water flows down along the slope and fills the mountain’s clefts, gullies, and creeks; these, becoming full, fill up the pools;
these, becoming full, fill up the lakes;
these, becoming full, fill up the streams;
these, becoming full, fill up the rivers;
and these, becoming full, fill up the great ocean;
thus there is nutriment for the great ocean,
and in this way it becomes full.

pali: evam evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappurisa-saṃsevo paripūro, saddhamma-ssavanaṃ paripūreti;
tīṇi sucaritāni paripūrāni, cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti;
cattāro satipaṭṭhānā paripūrā, satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti;
evam etissā vijjā-vimuttiyā āhāro hoti, evañ ca pāripūrī”ti.
en: So too, associating with good persons, becoming full, fills up hearing the good Dhamma….
The seven factors of enlightenment, becoming full,
fill up true knowledge and liberation.
Thus there is nutriment for true knowledge and liberation, and in this way they become full.”
‘All conditioned things are anicca’ —
when one sees this with wisdom,
one grows disenchanted with dukkha;
this is the path to purification.
‘All conditioned things are dukkha’ —
when one sees this with wisdom,
one grows disenchanted with dukkha;
this is the path to purification.
‘All things are nonself’ —
when one sees this with wisdom,
one grows disenchanted with dukkha;
this is the path to purification.
Those meditators, persevering,
constantly firm in their effort,
the wise touch nibbāna,
the unsurpassed security from bondage.
One is the pursuit of worldly gain,
and quite another is [the path] leading to nibbāna.
Clearly understanding this,
a bhikkhu, a disciple of the Buddha,
should not seek delight in honors,
but develop detachment instead.
Awake, always fully awake,
the disciples of Gotama,
whose minds delight in cultivation
both by day and by night.
Awake, always fully awake,
the disciples of Gotama,
whose awareness is constantly directed to the body,
both by day and by night.
Patience and endurance are the highest spiritual practices.
nibbāna is supreme, say the Buddhas.
One who harms others is not a true monk,
nor is one who oppresses others a true renunciate.
Not by mere vows or observing sīla, not by great learning, nor by the attainment of samādhi,
nor by dwelling in secluded places,
[not because it occurs to you,]
‘I experience the happiness of renunciation,
inaccessible to ordinary people.’
O bhikkhu, do not rest content so long as the destruction of the āsavas is not attained.
Impermanent, indeed, are conditioned things,
having the nature of arising and passing away;
having arisen, they cease,
their stilling is happiness.
The greatest of all gains is health;
nibbāna is the greatest happiness;
the eightfold [path is the greatest] of paths,
for it leads safely to the Deathless.

pali: ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto magadhesu viharati
en: On one occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling in Magadha at Nālakagāma.
Then the wanderer Jambukhādaka approached
the Venerable Sāriputta and exchanged
greetings with him.

pali: ekam antaṃ nisīdi. ekam antaṃ nisinno kho, jambukhādako paribbājako āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etad avoca:
en: When they had concluded their greetings and
cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to
the Venerable Sāriputta:
“Friend Sāriputta, it is said, ‘nibbāna, nibbāna.’
What now is nibbāna?”
“The destruction of craving, the destruction of aversion, the destruction of delusion:
this, friend, is called nibbāna.”

pali: “atthi pan’āvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa
“atthi kho, āvuso, maggo, atthi paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa
en: “But, friend, is there a path, is there a way for the realization of this nibbāna?”
“There is a path, friend,
there is a way for the realization of this nibbāna.”

pali: “katamo pan’āvuso, maggo, katamā paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa sacchi-kiriyāyā”ti?
en: “And what, friend, is that path,
what is that way for the realization of this nibbāna?”

pali: “ayameva kho, āvuso, ariyo aṭṭh’aṅgiko maggo etassa nibbānassa sacchi-kiriyāya, seyyath’idaṃ:
en: “It is, friend, this Noble Eightfold Path;
that is, right view, right intention,
right speech, right action, right livelihood,
right effort, right awareness, right concentration.

pali: ayaṃ kho, āvuso, maggo, ayaṃ paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa sacchi-kiriyāyā”ti.
en: This is the path, friend, this is the way for the realization of this nibbāna.”

pali: “bhaddako, āvuso, maggo, bhaddikā paṭipadā etassa nibbānassa sacchi-kiriyāya.
en: “Excellent is the path, friend, excellent is the way for the realization of this nibbāna. And it is sufficient,
friend Sāriputta, for [practicing with] diligence.”

pali: evaṃ me sutaṃ. ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jeta-vane, anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhū nibbāna-paṭisaṃyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti, samādapeti, samuttejeti, sampahaṃseti. te’dha bhikkhū aṭṭhiṃ katvā, manasi katvā, sabbaṃ cetaso samannāharitvā, ohita-sotā dhammaṃ suṇanti.
en: Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now on that occasion the Blessed One was instructing, inspiring, uplifting, and gladdening the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk connected with nibbāna. And those bhikkhus were listening to the Dhamma with eager ears, attending to it as a matter of vital concern, applying their whole mind to it.

pali: atha kho bhagavā etam atthaṃ viditvā, tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ udānaṃ udānesi:
en: Then, realizing the significance of this, the Blessed One on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

pali: “atthi, bhikkhave, ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akataṃ asaṅkhataṃ. no c’etaṃ, bhikkhave, abhavissa ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akataṃ asaṅkhataṃ, nayidha jātassa bhūtassa katassa saṅkhatassa nissaraṇaṃ paññāyetha.
en: “There is, bhikkhus, the unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned. If, bhikkhus, there were no unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, no escape would be discerned here from the born, become, made, conditioned.

pali: yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, atthi ajātaṃ abhūtaṃ akataṃ asaṅkhataṃ, tasmā jātassa bhūtassa katassa saṅkhatassa nissaraṇaṃ paññāyatī”ti.
en: But because there is an unborn, unbecome, unmade, unconditioned, an escape is discerned from the born, become, made, conditioned.”

suttas.title: dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā ariyasaccaṃ
suttas.en: The Noble Truth of the Way

en: “Now this, bhikkhus, is the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of dukkha:
it is this Noble Eightfold Path; that is,
right view, right intention,
right speech, right action, right livelihood,
right effort, right awareness, right concentration.”

pali: sāvatthi-nidānaṃ. “ariyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, aṭṭh’aṅgikaṃ maggaṃ desessāmi vibhajissāmi. taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti.
“evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. bhagavā etad avoca:
en: At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Noble Eightfold Path and I will analyze it for you. Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.”
“Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied. The Blessed One said this:

pali: “katamo ca, bhikkhave, ariyo aṭṭh’aṅgiko maggo? seyyath’idaṃ: sammā-diṭṭhi … pe … sammā-samādhi.
en: “And what, bhikkhus, is the Noble Eightfold Path? Right view … right concentration.

pali: katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammā-diṭṭhi? yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dukkhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkha-samudaye ñāṇaṃ, dukkha-nirodhe ñāṇaṃ, dukkha-nirodha-gāminiyā paṭipadāya ñāṇaṃ — ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammā-diṭṭhi.
en: And what, bhikkhus, is right view? Knowledge of dukkha, knowledge of the origin of dukkha, knowledge of the cessation of dukkha, knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of dukkha: this is called right view.

pali: katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammā-saṅkappo? yo kho, bhikkhave, nekkhamma-saṅkappo, abyāpāda-saṅkappo, avihiṃsā-saṅkappo — ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammā-saṅkappo.
en: And what, bhikkhus, is right intention? Intention of renunciation, intention of non-ill will, intention of harmlessness: this is called right intention.

pali: katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammā-vācā? yā kho, bhikkhave, musā-vādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, sampha-ppalāpā veramaṇī — ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammā-vācā.
en: And what, bhikkhus, is right speech? Abstinence from false speech, abstinence from divisive speech, abstinence from harsh speech, abstinence from idle chatter: this is called right speech.

pali: katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammā-kammanto? yā kho, bhikkhave, pāṇ’ātipātā veramaṇī, adinn’ādānā veramaṇī, abrahma-cariyā veramaṇī — ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammā-kammanto.
en: And what, bhikkhus, is right action? Abstinence from the destruction of life, abstinence from taking what is not given, abstinence from sexual misconduct: this is called right action.

pali: katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammā-ājīvo? idha, bhikkhave, ariya-sāvako micchā-ājīvaṃ pahāya sammā-ājīvena jīvitaṃ kappeti — ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammā-ājīvo.
en: And what, bhikkhus, is right livelihood? Here a noble disciple, having abandoned a wrong mode of livelihood, earns his living by a right livelihood: this is called right livelihood.

pali: katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammā-vāyāmo? idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti, vāyamati, vīriyaṃ ārabhati, cittaṃ paggaṇhāti, padahati; uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti … pe … anuppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ uppādāya chandaṃ janeti … pe … uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā, asammosāya, bhiyyo-bhāvāya, vepullāya, bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṃ janeti, vāyamati, vīriyaṃ ārabhati, cittaṃ paggaṇhāti, padahati — ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammā-vāyāmo.
en: And what, bhikkhus, is right effort? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen bad unwholesome states; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives. He generates desire for the abandoning of arisen bad unwholesome states … He generates desire for the arising of unarisen wholesome states … He generates desire for the maintenance of arisen wholesome states, for their non-decay, increase, expansion, and fulfillment by development; he makes an effort, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives. This is called right effort.

pali: katamā ca, bhikkhave, sammā-sati? idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāy’ānupassī viharati, ātāpī, sampajāno, satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhā-domanassaṃ; vedanāsu vedan’ānupassī viharati … pe … citte citt’ānupassī viharati … pe … dhammesu dhamm’ānupassī viharati, ātāpī, sampajāno, satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhā-domanassaṃ — ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammā-sati.
en: And what, bhikkhus, is right awareness? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells observing the body as body, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware, having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world. He dwells observing vedanā as vedanā … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware, having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world. This is called right awareness.

pali: katamo ca, bhikkhave, sammā-samādhi? idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicc’eva kāmehi, vivicca akusalehi dhammehi, sa-vitakkaṃ sa-vicāraṃ viveka-jaṃ pīti-sukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. vitakka-vicārānaṃ vūpasamā ajjhattaṃ sampasādanaṃ cetaso ekodi-bhāvaṃ avitakkaṃ avicāraṃ samādhi-jaṃ pīti-sukhaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.
en: And what, bhikkhus, is right concentration? Here, bhikkhus, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a bhikkhu enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by thought and examination, with rapture and happiness born of seclusion. With the subsiding of thought and examination, he enters and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and unification of mind, is without thought and examination, and has rapture and happiness born of concentration.

pali: pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati, sato ca sampajāno, sukhañ ca kāyena paṭisaṃvedeti, yaṃ taṃ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukha-vihārī’ti tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. sukhassa ca pahānā, dukkhassa ca pahānā, pubb’eva somanassa-domanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā, adukkham-asukhaṃ upekkhā-sati-pārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati — ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sammā-samādhī”ti.
en: With the fading away as well of rapture, he dwells equanimous and, aware and clearly comprehending, he experiences pleasure with the body; he enters and dwells in the third jhāna of which the noble ones declare: ‘He is equanimous, aware, one who dwells happily.’ With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous passing away of joy and displeasure, he enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is neither painful nor pleasant and includes the purification of awareness by equanimity. This is called right concentration.”

suttas.title: brahmacariyaṃ sāraṃ
suttas.en: The Heartwood of the Spiritual Life

pali: yā ca kho ayaṃ, bhikkhave, akuppā ceto-vimutti —
en: “… So, this spiritual life, bhikkhus, does not have gain, honor, and renown for its benefit,
nor the attainment of virtue for its benefit,
nor the attainment of concentration for its benefit,
nor knowledge and vision for its benefit.
But it is this unshakeable deliverance of mind that is the goal of this spiritual life, its heartwood, and its end.”
At Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unconditioned
and the path leading to the unconditioned. Listen to that.
And what, bhikkhus, is the unconditioned?
The destruction of craving, the destruction of aversion,
the destruction of delusion:
this is called the unconditioned.
And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned? Awareness directed to the body:
this is called the path leading to the unconditioned.

pali: iti kho, bhikkhave, desitaṃ vo mayā asaṅkhataṃ,
yaṃ, bhikkhave, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hit’esinā anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya,
en: Thus, bhikkhus, I have taught you the unconditioned
and the path leading to the unconditioned.
Whatever should be done, bhikkhus, by a compassionate teacher out of compassion for his disciples,
desiring their welfare, that I have done for you.
These are the feet of trees, bhikkhus, these are empty huts. Meditate, bhikkhus, do not be negligent,
lest you regret it later.
This is our instruction to you.”

pali: ‘kāya-gatā no sati bhāvitā bhavissati bahulī-katā, yānī-katā,
en: “… Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will develop and cultivate awareness directed
to the body, make it our vehicle, make it our basis,
stabilize it, exercise ourselves in it, and fully undertake it.’ Thus should you train yourselves.”
At Sāvatthī.
There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:
“Bhikkhus, on one occasion I was dwelling at Uruvelā on the bank of the river Nerañjarā, under the Goatherd’s Banyan Tree just after I became fully enlightened.

Then, while I was alone in seclusion, a reflection arose in my mind thus: ‘This is the direct path for the purification of beings, for the overcoming of sorrow and lamentation, for the passing away of pain and dejection, for the achievement of the method,
for the realization of nibbāna,
that is, the four establishments of awareness.’”
At Sāvatthī.
“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell aware and clearly comprehending. This is our instruction to you.

pali: kathañ ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sato hoti?
idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāy’ānupassī viharati,
en: And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu aware?
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells observing the body as body, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware,
having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.

pali: vedanāsu vedan’ānupassī viharati, ātāpī, sampajāno, satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhā-domanassaṃ.
citte citt’ānupassī viharati, ātāpī, sampajāno, satimā,
dhammesu dhamm’ānupassī viharati, ātāpī, sampajāno, satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhā-domanassaṃ.
evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sato hoti.
en: … vedanā as vedanā, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware, having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.
… mind as mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware,
having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.
… phenomena as phenomena, ardent,
clearly comprehending, aware,
having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.
It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is aware.

pali: kathañ ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sampajāno hoti?
en: And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu clearly comprehend?
Here, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu
vedanā are understood as they arise,
understood as they remain present,
understood as they pass away.
Thoughts are understood as they arise,
understood as they remain present,
understood as they pass away.
Perceptions are understood as they arise,
understood as they remain present,
understood as they pass away.

pali: evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sampajāno hoti.
en: It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu clearly comprehends. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu should dwell aware and clearly comprehending. This is our instruction to you.”

pali: “kathañ ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāy’ānupassī viharati? idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu arañña-gato vā,
rukkha-mūla-gato vā, suññ’āgāra-gato vā nisīdati; pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā, ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya,
en: “And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu dwell observing body as body? Here a bhikkhu, gone to the forest or to the foot of a tree or to an empty hut, sits down;
having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect,
and established awareness around the mouth,
just aware, he breathes in; just aware, he breathes out.

pali: dīghaṃ vā assasanto, ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti, dīghaṃ vā passasanto, ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti, rassaṃ vā assasanto, ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti,
en: Breathing in long, he understands: ‘I breathe in long’; or breathing out long, he understands: ‘I breathe out long.’ Breathing in short, he understands: ‘I breathe in short’; or breathing out short, he understands: ‘I breathe out short.’

pali: ‘sabba-kāya-paṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ kāya-saṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati, ‘passambhayaṃ kāya-saṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati.”
en: He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the whole body’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body.’ He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in tranquilizing the bodily formation’; he trains thus:
‘I shall breathe out tranquilizing the bodily formation.’”

pali: ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā icchānaṅgale viharati icchānaṅgala-vana-saṇḍe. tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi: “icchām’ahaṃ, bhikkhave, te-māsaṃ paṭisallīyituṃ. n’āmhi kenaci upasaṅkamitabbo, aññatra ekena piṇḍa-pāta-nīhārakenā”ti.
en: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Icchānaṅgala in the Icchānaṅgala Wood. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus: “Bhikkhus, I wish to go into seclusion for three months. I should not be approached by anyone except the one who brings me almsfood.”

pali: “evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paṭissutvā n’āssudha koci bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamati, aññatra ekena piṇḍa-pāta-nīhārakena.
en: “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied, and no one approached the Blessed One except the one who brought him almsfood.

pali: atha kho bhagavā tassa te-māsassa accayena paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito bhikkhū āmantesi: “sace kho, bhikkhave, añña-titthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ: ‘katamen’āvuso, vihārena samaṇo gotamo vassāvāsaṃ bahulaṃ vihāsī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ añña-titthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha: ‘ānāpāna-ssati-samādhinā kho, āvuso, bhagavā vassāvāsaṃ bahulaṃ vihāsī’ti.
en: Then, when those three months had passed, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and addressed the bhikkhus thus: “Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects ask you: ‘In what dwelling, friends, did the Blessed One generally dwell during the rains residence?’ — being asked thus, you should answer those wanderers thus: ‘During the rains residence, friends, the Blessed One generally dwelt in the concentration by awareness of breathing.’

pali: idh’āhaṃ, bhikkhave, sato assasāmi, sato passasāmi. dīghaṃ assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāmi, dīghaṃ passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāmi; rassaṃ assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāmi, rassaṃ passasanto ‘rassaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāmi; ‘sabba-kāya-ppaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti pajānāmi … pe … ‘paṭinissagg’ānupassī passasissāmī’ti pajānāmi.
en: Here, bhikkhus, aware I breathe in, aware I breathe out. When breathing in long I know: ‘I breathe in long’; when breathing out long I know: ‘I breathe out long.’ When breathing in short I know: ‘I breathe in short’; when breathing out short I know: ‘I breathe out short.’ I know: ‘Experiencing the whole body I will breathe in’ … I know: ‘Observing relinquishment, I will breathe out.’

pali: yañ hi taṃ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya: ‘ariya-vihāro’ iti’pi, ‘brahma-vihāro’ iti’pi, ‘tathāgata-vihāro’ iti’pi, ānāpāna-ssati-samādhiṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya: ‘ariya-vihāro’ iti’pi, ‘brahma-vihāro’ iti’pi, ‘tathāgata-vihāro’ iti’pi.
en: If anyone, bhikkhus, speaking rightly could say of anything: ‘It is a noble dwelling, a divine dwelling, the Tathāgata’s dwelling,’ it is of concentration by awareness of breathing that one could rightly say this.

pali: ye te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū sekhā appatta-mānasā anuttaraṃ yoga-kkhemaṃ patthayamānā viharanti, tesaṃ ānāpāna-ssati-samādhi bhāvito bahulī-kato āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattati.
en: Bhikkhus, those bhikkhus who are trainees, who have not attained their mind’s ideal, who dwell aspiring for the unsurpassed security from bondage: for them concentration by awareness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, leads to the destruction of the āsavas.

pali: ye ca kho te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū arahanto khīṇ’āsavā vusitavanto kata-karaṇīyā ohita-bhārā anuppatta-sad-atthā parikkhīṇa-bhava-saṃyojanā sammadaññā vimuttā, tesaṃ ānāpāna-ssati-samādhi bhāvito bahulī-kato diṭṭha-dhamma-sukha-vihārāya c’eva saṃvattati sati-sampajaññāya ca.
en: Those bhikkhus who are arahants, whose āsavas are destroyed, who have lived the spiritual life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, reached their own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, those completely liberated through final knowledge: for them concentration by awareness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, leads to a pleasant dwelling in this very life and to awareness and clear comprehension.

pali: yañ hi taṃ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya: ‘ariya-vihāro’ iti’pi, ‘brahma-vihāro’ iti’pi, ‘tathāgata-vihāro’ iti’pi, ānāpāna-ssati-samādhiṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya: ‘ariya-vihāro’ iti’pi, ‘brahma-vihāro’ iti’pi, ‘tathāgata-vihāro’ iti’pī”ti.
en: If anyone, bhikkhus, speaking rightly could say of anything: ‘It is a noble dwelling, a divine dwelling, the Tathāgata’s dwelling,’ it is of concentration by awareness of breathing that one could rightly say this.”

pali: sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkham-asukhā vedanā.
imāsaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tissannaṃ vedanānaṃ pariññāya
en: “Bhikkhus, there are these three vedanā.
What three? Pleasant vedanā, painful vedanā,
neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā.
These are the three vedanā.
The four establishments of awareness are to be developed for the full understanding of these three vedanā.”

pali: “kathañ ca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vedanāsu vedan’ānupassī viharati? idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sukhaṃ vā vedanaṃ vedayamāno,
en: “And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu dwell observing vedanā as vedanā? Here, when feeling a pleasant vedanā, a bhikkhu understands: ‘I feel a pleasant vedanā’;
when feeling a painful vedanā, he understands:
‘I feel a painful vedanā’;
when feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā,
he understands: ‘I feel a neither-painful-nor-pleasant vedanā.’…”

pali: “kathañ ca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu citte citt’ānupassī viharati? idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu
en: “And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu dwell observing
mind as mind? Here, a bhikkhu understands
mind with craving as mind with craving,
and mind without craving as mind without craving.
He understands mind with aversion as mind with aversion, and mind without aversion as mind without aversion.
He understands mind with delusion as mind with delusion, and mind without delusion as mind without delusion…”

pali: imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ pahānāya cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvetabbā.”
en: “Bhikkhus, there are these five hindrances. What five? The hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill-will, the hindrance of dullness and drowsiness,
the hindrance of restlessness and remorse,
and the hindrance of doubt.
These are the five hindrances.
The four establishments of awareness are to be developed for abandoning these five hindrances.”

pali: kathañ ca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhamm’ānupassī viharati pañcasu nīvaraṇesu?
en: “And how, bhikkhus, does a bhikkhu dwell observing phenomena as phenomena?
Here a bhikkhu dwells observing phenomena as phenomena in regard to the five hindrances.
And how does a bhikkhu dwell observing phenomena as phenomena in regard to the five hindrances?

pali: idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ
kāma-cchandaṃ, ‘atthi me ajjhattaṃ kāma-cchando’ti pajānāti; asantaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ kāma-cchandaṃ,
en: Here, there being sensual desire in him, a bhikkhu understands: ‘There is sensual desire in me’;
or there being no sensual desire in him,
he understands: ‘There is no sensual desire in me’;

pali: yathā ca anuppannassa kāma-cchandassa uppādo hoti,
tañ ca pajānāti; yathā ca uppannassa kāma-cchandassa pahānaṃ hoti, tañ ca pajānāti; yathā ca pahīnassa
kāma-cchandassa āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti, tañ ca pajānāti.
… pe … ‘atthi me ajjhattaṃ byāpādo’ti pajānāti … pe … ‘atthi me ajjhattaṃ thina-middhan’ti pajānāti …
en: and he also understands how there comes to be the arising of unarisen sensual desire, and how there comes to be the abandoning of arisen sensual desire, and how there comes to be the future non-arising of abandoned sensual desire.
… He understands: ‘There is ill-will in me’ …
He understands: ‘There is dullness and drowsiness in me’ …
He understands: ‘There is restlessness and remorse in me’ …

pali: santaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ vicikicchaṃ, ‘atthi me ajjhattaṃ vicikicchā’ti pajānāti; asantaṃ vā ajjhattaṃ vicikicchaṃ, ‘n’atthi me ajjhattaṃ vicikicchā’ti pajānāti;
yathā ca anuppannāya vicikicchāya uppādo hoti,
tañ ca pajānāti; yathā ca uppannāya vicikicchāya pahānaṃ hoti, tañ ca pajānāti; yathā ca pahīnāya vicikicchāya āyatiṃ anuppādo hoti, tañ ca pajānāti.
en: There being doubt in him, a bhikkhu understands:
‘There is doubt in me’; or there being no doubt in him,
he understands: ‘There is no doubt in me’;
and he understands how there comes to be the arising of unarisen doubt, and how there comes to be the abandoning of arisen doubt,
and how there comes to be the future non-arising of abandoned doubt.

pali: iti ajjhattaṃ vā dhammesu dhamm’ānupassī viharati,
en: In this way he dwells observing phenomena as phenomena internally, or he dwells observing phenomena as phenomena externally, or he dwells observing phenomena as phenomena both internally and externally.

Or he dwells observing in phenomena their nature of arising, or he dwells observing in phenomena their nature of vanishing, or he dwells observing in phenomena their nature of both arising and vanishing.

pali: ‘atthi dhammā’ti vā pan’assa sati paccupaṭṭhitā hoti
anissito ca viharati, na ca kiñci loke upādiyati.
evam’pi kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammesu dhamm’ānupassī viharati pañcasu nīvaraṇesu.”
en: Or else awareness that ‘there are phenomena’
is simply established in him to the extent necessary for bare knowledge and awareness. And he abides independent, not clinging to anything in the world.
That is how a bhikkhu dwells observing phenomena as phenomena in regard to the five hindrances.”

“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the establishment of awareness, and the development of the establishment of awareness, and the way leading to the development of the establishment of awareness. Listen to that.

pali: idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāy’ānupassī viharati, ātāpī,
en: And what, bhikkhus, is the establishment of awareness? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells observing the body as body, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware, having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.
He dwells observing vedanā as vedanā …
mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware,
having removed craving and aversion in regard
to the world.
This is called the establishment of awareness.
