And what, bhikkhus, is the development of the establishment of awareness? Here, bhikkhus,

a bhikkhu dwells observing the nature of origination in the body; he dwells observing the nature of vanishing in the body; he dwells observing the nature of origination and vanishing in the body — ardent,
clearly comprehending, aware, having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.

He dwells observing the nature of origination in vedanā … He dwells observing the nature of origination in mind … He dwells observing the nature of origination in phenomena; he dwells observing the nature of vanishing in phenomena;

he dwells observing the nature of origination and vanishing in phenomena — ardent, clearly comprehending, aware, having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world. This is called the development of the establishment of awareness.
And what, bhikkhus, is the way leading to the development of the establishment of awareness?
It is this Noble Eightfold Path; that is,
right view, right intention,
right speech, right action, right livelihood,
right effort, right awareness, right concentration.
This is called the way leading to the development of the establishment of awareness.”
“… Therefore, Ānanda, dwell with yourselves as your
own island, with yourselves as your own refuge,
with no other refuge; dwell with the Dhamma as your island, with the Dhamma as your refuge,
with no other refuge.
And how, Ānanda, does a bhikkhu dwell with himself as
his own island, with himself as his own refuge,
with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island,
with the Dhamma as his refuge, with no other refuge?

pali: dhammesu dhamm’ānupassī viharati, ātāpī, sampajāno, satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhā-domanassaṃ.
en: Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells observing the body as body,
ardent, clearly comprehending, aware,
having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.
He dwells observing vedanā as vedanā …
mind as mind …
phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, aware, having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world.

pali: evaṃ kho, ānanda, bhikkhu atta-dīpo viharati,
en: It is in this way, Ānanda, that a bhikkhu dwells with
himself as his own island, with himself as his own refuge,
with no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island,
with the Dhamma as his refuge, with no other refuge. …”
“Venerable sir, it is said,
‘Factors of enlightenment, factors of enlightenment.’
In what sense are they called factors of enlightenment?”
“‘They lead to enlightenment,’ bhikkhu,
therefore they are called ‘factors of enlightenment.’”

“Bhikkhus, when awareness of breathing is developed and cultivated, it is of great fruit and great benefit. When awareness of breathing is developed and cultivated, it fulfills the four establishments of awareness. When the four establishments of awareness are developed and cultivated,
they fulfill the seven enlightenment factors.
When the seven enlightenment factors are developed and cultivated, they fulfill true knowledge and liberation. […]

pali: kathaṃ bhāvitā ca, bhikkhave, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā
yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāy’ānupassī (vedanāsu vedan’ānupassī… citte citt’ānupassī… dhammesu dhamm’ānupassī) viharati, ātāpī, sampajāno, satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhā-domanassaṃ,
upaṭṭhitā’ssa tasmiṃ samaye sati hoti asammuṭṭhā.
en: And how, bhikkhus, do the four establishments of awareness, developed and cultivated, fulfill the seven enlightenment factors? Bhikkhus, on whatever occasion a bhikkhu dwells observing the body as body (vedanā as vedanā… mind as mind… phenomena as phenomena), ardent, clearly comprehending, and aware,
having removed craving and aversion in regard to the world — on that occasion unremitting awareness is established in him.

pali: yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno upaṭṭhitā sati hoti asammuṭṭhā, sati-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye
en: On whatever occasion unremitting awareness is established in a bhikkhu — on that occasion the awareness enlightenment factor is aroused in him,
and he develops it, and by development,
it comes to fulfillment in him.

pali: so tathā-sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati, pavicayati, parivīmaṃsaṃ āpajjati.
yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathā-sato viharanto taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinati, pavicayati, parivīmaṃsaṃ āpajjati,
en: Abiding thus aware, he investigates and examines
that dhamma with wisdom,
and engages in a full exploration of it.
On whatever occasion, abiding thus aware,
a bhikkhu investigates and examines that dhamma with wisdom, and engages in a full exploration of it —

pali: dhamma-vicaya-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanā-pāripūriṃ gacchati.
en: on that occasion the investigation of reality enlightenment factor is aroused in him,
and he develops it,
and by development it comes to fulfillment in him.

pali: tassa taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato, pavicayato, parivīmaṃsaṃ āpajjato, āraddhaṃ hoti vīriyaṃ asallīnaṃ. yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno taṃ dhammaṃ paññāya pavicinato, pavicayato, parivīmaṃsaṃ āpajjato, āraddhaṃ hoti vīriyaṃ asallīnaṃ, vīriya-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti,
vīriya-sambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, vīriya-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno
en: In one who investigates and examines that dhamma with wisdom and embarks upon a full inquiry into it, tireless energy is aroused.
On whatever occasion tireless energy is aroused in
a bhikkhu who investigates and examines that dhamma with wisdom and embarks upon a full inquiry into it —
on that occasion the energy enlightenment factor is aroused in him, and he develops it,
and by development it comes to fulfillment in him.

pali: āraddha-vīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā. yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno āraddha-vīriyassa uppajjati pīti nirāmisā, pīti-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, pīti-sambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, pīti-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanā-pāripūriṃ gacchati.
en: In one who has aroused energy, unworldly rapture arises. On whatever occasion unworldly rapture arises in a bhikkhu who has aroused energy —
on that occasion the rapture enlightenment factor is aroused in him, and he develops it,
and by development it comes to fulfillment in him.

pali: pīti-manassa kāyo’pi passambhati, cittam’pi passambhati. yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno pīti-manassa kāyo’pi passambhati, cittam’pi passambhati,
passaddhi-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, passaddhi-sambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti,
passaddhi-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanā-pāripūriṃ gacchati.
en: For one with a rapturous mind, the body and the mind become tranquil. On whatever occasion the body and the mind become tranquil in a bhikkhu with a rapturous mind — on that occasion the tranquility enlightenment factor is aroused in him, and he develops it,
and by development it comes to fulfillment in him.

pali: yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno passaddha-kāyassa sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati, samādhi-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti,
samādhi-sambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, samādhi-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno bhāvanā-pāripūriṃ gacchati.
en: In one whose body is tranquil and who feels pleasure, the mind becomes concentrated.
On whatever occasion the mind becomes concentrated in a bhikkhu whose body is tranquil and who feels pleasure — on that occasion the concentration enlightenment factor is aroused in him,
and he develops it,
and by development it comes to fulfillment in him.

pali: so tathā-samāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti. yasmiṃ samaye, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathā-samāhitaṃ cittaṃ sādhukaṃ ajjhupekkhitā hoti,
upekkhā-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhuno āraddho hoti, upekkhā-sambojjhaṅgaṃ tasmiṃ samaye bhikkhu bhāveti, upekkhā-sambojjhaṅgo tasmiṃ samaye
en: He closely looks on with equanimity at the mind thus concentrated.
On whatever occasion a bhikkhu closely looks on with equanimity at the mind thus concentrated —
on that occasion the equanimity enlightenment factor is aroused in him, and he develops it,
and by development it comes to fulfillment in him. […]

pali: evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā evaṃ bahulī-katā satta sambojjhaṅge paripūrenti.”
en: Bhikkhus, that is how the four establishments of awareness, developed and cultivated,
fulfill the seven enlightenment factors.”

suttas.title: jentātherīgāthā
suttas.en: Verse of the Elder Bhikkhunī Jentā

en: “These seven factors of enlightenment
are the path to attaining nibbāna.
They are all developed by me,
just as taught by the Buddha.”

pali: “n’āhaṃ, bhikkhave, ādikeneva aññ’ārādhanaṃ vadāmi; api ca, bhikkhave, anupubba-sikkhā, anupubba-kiriyā, anupubba-paṭipadā, aññ’ārādhanā hoti.
en: “Bhikkhus, I do not say that final knowledge is achieved all at once. On the contrary, final knowledge is achieved by gradual training, by gradual practice, by gradual progress.
And how is final knowledge achieved by gradual training, gradual practice, gradual progress?

pali: idha, bhikkhave, saddhā-jāto upasaṅkamati; upasaṅkamanto, payirupāsati;
atthaṃ upaparikkhato, dhammā nijjhānaṃ khamanti; dhamma-nijjhāna-kkhantiyā sati, chando jāyati;
en: Here, one who has faith [in a teacher] visits him;
when he visits him, he pays respect to him;
when he pays respect to him, he gives ear;
one who gives ear hears the Dhamma;
having heard the Dhamma, he memorizes it;
he examines the meaning of the teachings he has memorized; when he examines their meaning,
he gains a reflective acceptance of those teachings;

when he has gained a reflective acceptance of those teachings, zeal springs up in him; when zeal has sprung up, he applies his will; having applied his will, he scrutinizes; having scrutinized, he strives; resolutely striving,
he realizes with the body the supreme truth,
and sees it by penetrating it with wisdom.”
“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unconditioned and
the path leading to the unconditioned. Listen to that.
And what, bhikkhus, is the unconditioned?
The destruction of craving, the destruction of aversion, the destruction of delusion: this is called the unconditioned.

pali: idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janeti;
vāyamati, vīriyaṃ ārabhati, cittaṃ paggaṇhāti, padahati. […]
en: And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu generates desire for the non-arising of unarisen bad unwholesome states;
he makes an effort, arouses energy,
applies his mind, and strives […]

pali: uppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya chandaṃ janeti; vāyamati, vīriyaṃ ārabhati,
en: He generates desire for the abandoning of arisen bad unwholesome states; he makes an effort,
arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives. […]
He generates desire for the arising of unarisen
wholesome states; he makes an effort,
arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives. […]

pali: uppannānaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ ṭhitiyā, asammosāya, bhiyyo-bhāvāya, vepullāya,
en: He generates desire for the continuance of arisen wholesome states, for their non-decay, increase, expansion, and fulfillment by development;
he makes an effort, arouses energy,
applies his mind, and strives:
this is called the path leading to the unconditioned.

pali: iti kho, bhikkhave, desitaṃ vo mayā asaṅkhataṃ,
yaṃ, bhikkhave, satthārā karaṇīyaṃ sāvakānaṃ hit’esinā anukampakena anukampaṃ upādāya,
en: Thus, bhikkhus, I have taught you the unconditioned and the path leading to the unconditioned.
Whatever should be done, bhikkhus,
by a compassionate teacher out of compassion
for his disciples, desiring their welfare,
that I have done for you.
These are the feet of trees, bhikkhus, these are empty huts. Meditate, bhikkhus, do not be negligent,
lest you regret it later.
This is our instruction to you.”

pali: “taṃ kiṃ maññasi, soṇa, kusalo tvaṃ pubbe agāriya-bhūto vīṇāya tanti-ssare”ti?
en: “Tell me, Soṇa, in the past, when you lived at home, weren’t you skilled at the lute?”
“Yes, venerable sir.”

pali: “taṃ kiṃ maññasi, soṇa, yadā te vīṇāya tantiyo accāyatā honti, api nu te vīṇā tasmiṃ samaye saravatī vā hoti kammaññā vā”ti?
en: “What do you think, Soṇa?
When its strings were too tight,
was your lute well tuned and easy to play?”
“No, venerable sir.”

pali: “taṃ kiṃ maññasi, soṇa, yadā te vīṇāya tantiyo atisithilā honti, api nu te vīṇā tasmiṃ samaye saravatī vā hoti kammaññā vā”ti?
en: “When its strings were too loose,
was your lute well tuned and easy to play?”
“No, venerable sir.”

pali: “yadā pana te, soṇa, vīṇāya tantiyo na accāyatā honti n’ātisithilā same guṇe patiṭṭhitā, api nu te vīṇā tasmiṃ samaye saravatī vā hoti kammaññā vā”ti?
en: “But, Soṇa, when its strings were neither too tight
nor too loose but adjusted to a balanced pitch,
was your lute well tuned and easy to play?”
“Yes, venerable sir.”
“So too, Soṇa,
overly aroused effort leads to restlessness,
and overly lax effort leads to laziness.

pali: tasmātiha tvaṃ, soṇa, vīriya-samathaṃ adhiṭṭhahaṃ, indriyānañ ca samataṃ paṭivijjha,
en: Therefore, Soṇa, resolve on relaxed effort,
find the balance of the spiritual faculties,
and take up the object there.”

suttas.title: eseva maggo bodhāya
suttas.en: That Is the Path to Enlightenment

pali: “… na kho pan’āhaṃ imāya kaṭukāya dukkara-kārikāya adhigacchāmi uttari manussa-dhammā alam-ariya-ñāṇa-dassana-visesaṃ. siyā nu kho añño maggo bodhāyā’ti?
en: “… But by this racking practice of austerities I have not attained any superhuman states, any distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones. Could there be another path to enlightenment?’

pali: tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etad ahosi: ‘abhijānāmi kho pan’āhaṃ pitu sakkassa kammante sītāya jambu-cchāyāya nisinno vivicc’eva kāmehi, vivicca akusalehi dhammehi, sa-vitakkaṃ sa-vicāraṃ viveka-jaṃ pīti-sukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharitā. siyā nu kho eso maggo bodhāyā’ti?
en: I considered: ‘I recall that when my father the Sakyan was occupied, while I was sitting in the cool shade of a rose-apple tree, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I entered upon and abided in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. Could that be the path to enlightenment?’

pali: tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, sat’ānusāri viññāṇaṃ ahosi: ‘es’eva maggo bodhāyā’ti.
en: Then, following on that memory, came the realization: ‘That is indeed the path to enlightenment.’

pali: tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etad ahosi: ‘kiṃ nu kho ahaṃ tassa sukhassa bhāyāmi, yaṃ taṃ sukhaṃ aññatr’eva kāmehi, aññatra akusalehi dhammehī’ti?
tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etad ahosi: ‘na kho ahaṃ tassa sukhassa bhāyāmi, yaṃ taṃ sukhaṃ aññatr’eva kāmehi, aññatra akusalehi dhammehī’ti.
en: I thought: ‘Why am I afraid of that pleasure that has nothing to do with sensual pleasures and unwholesome states?’
I thought: ‘I am not afraid of that pleasure since it has nothing to do with sensual pleasures and unwholesome states.’

pali: tassa mayhaṃ, aggivessana, etad ahosi: ‘na kho taṃ sukaraṃ sukhaṃ adhigantuṃ evaṃ adhimattaka-simānaṃ patta-kāyena. yaṃ nūn’āhaṃ oḷārikaṃ āhāraṃ āhāreyyaṃ odana-kummāsan’ti. …
en: I considered: ‘It is not easy to attain that pleasure with a body so excessively emaciated. Suppose I ate some solid food — some boiled rice and porridge.’ …

pali: so kho ahaṃ, aggivessana, oḷārikaṃ āhāraṃ āhāretvā, balaṃ gahetvā, vivicc’eva kāmehi, vivicca akusalehi dhammehi, sa-vitakkaṃ sa-vicāraṃ viveka-jaṃ pīti-sukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. eva’rūpā’pi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati … pe … catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja vihāsiṃ. eva’rūpā’pi kho me, aggivessana, uppannā sukhā vedanā cittaṃ na pariyādāya tiṭṭhati.”
en: Now when I had eaten solid food and regained my strength, then quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, I entered upon and abided in the first jhāna … But such pleasant vedanā that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain … I entered upon and abided in the fourth jhāna. But such pleasant vedanā that arose in me did not invade my mind and remain.”

pali: “‘sukha-vinicchayaṃ jaññā; sukha-vinicchayaṃ ñatvā, ajjhattaṃ sukham anuyuñjeyyā’ti — iti kho pan’etaṃ vuttaṃ. kiñ c’etaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ?
en: “‘One should know how to define pleasure, and knowing that, one should pursue pleasure within oneself.’ So it was said. And with reference to what was this said?

pali: pañc’ime, bhikkhave, kāma-guṇā. katame pañca? cakkhu-viññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā, kantā, manāpā, piya-rūpā, kām’ūpasaṃhitā, rajanīyā; sota-viññeyyā saddā … ghāna-viññeyyā gandhā … jivhā-viññeyyā rasā … kāya-viññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā, kantā, manāpā, piya-rūpā, kām’ūpasaṃhitā, rajanīyā — ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca kāma-guṇā.
en: Bhikkhus, there are these five cords of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye … sounds cognizable by the ear … odors cognizable by the nose … flavors cognizable by the tongue … tangibles cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of craving. These are the five cords of sensual pleasure.

pali: yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ime pañca kāma-guṇe paṭicca uppajjati sukhaṃ somanassaṃ, idaṃ vuccati kāma-sukhaṃ, mīḷha-sukhaṃ, puthujjana-sukhaṃ, anariya-sukhaṃ. ‘na āsevitabbaṃ, na bhāvetabbaṃ, na bahulī-kātabbaṃ, bhāyitabbaṃ etassa sukhassā’ti vadāmi.
en: Now the pleasure and joy that arise dependent on these five cords of sensual pleasure are called sensual pleasure — a filthy pleasure, a coarse pleasure, an ignoble pleasure. I say of this kind of pleasure that it should not be pursued, that it should not be developed, that it should not be cultivated, and that it should be feared.

pali: idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicc’eva kāmehi, vivicca akusalehi dhammehi, sa-vitakkaṃ sa-vicāraṃ viveka-jaṃ pīti-sukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ … dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ … tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ … catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati.
en: Here, bhikkhus, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first jhāna … the second jhāna … the third jhāna … the fourth jhāna.

pali: idaṃ vuccati nekkhamma-sukhaṃ, paviveka-sukhaṃ, upasama-sukhaṃ, sambodhi-sukhaṃ. ‘āsevitabbaṃ, bhāvetabbaṃ, bahulī-kātabbaṃ, na bhāyitabbaṃ etassa sukhassā’ti vadāmi.
en: This is called the bliss of renunciation, the bliss of seclusion, the bliss of peace, the bliss of enlightenment. I say of this kind of pleasure that it should be pursued, that it should be developed, that it should be cultivated, and that it should not be feared.

pali: ‘sukha-vinicchayaṃ jaññā; sukha-vinicchayaṃ ñatvā, ajjhattaṃ sukham anuyuñjeyyā’ti — iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idam etaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.”
en: So it was with reference to this that it was said: ‘One should know how to define pleasure, and knowing that, one should pursue pleasure within oneself.’”

pali: mahā-vane, kūṭ’āgāra-sālāyaṃ. atha kho mahāpajāpatī gotamī yena bhagavā ten’upasaṅkami;
en: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī,
in the hall with the peaked roof in the Great Wood.
Then Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī approached the Blessed One,

pali: ekam antaṃ aṭṭhāsi. ekam antaṃ ṭhitā kho,
sā mahāpajāpatī gotamī bhagavantaṃ etad avoca:
en: paid homage to him, stood to one side, and said to him:

pali: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena dhammaṃ desetu, yam ahaṃ bhagavato dhammaṃ sutvā,
en: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach
me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute.”
“Gotamī, those things of which you might know:
‘These things lead (1) to craving, not to the fading away
of craving; (2) to bondage, not to non-attachment;
(3) to accumulating, not to discarding;
(4) to many desires, not to fewness of desires;
(5) to lack of contentment, not to contentment;
(6) to socializing, not to solitude;
(7) to laziness, not to the arousing of energy;
(8) to being difficult to support, not to being easy to support,’
you should bear in mind, Gotamī, certainly:
‘This is not the Dhamma; this is not the discipline;
this is not the teaching of the Teacher.’

pali: ye ca kho tvaṃ, gotami, dhamme jāneyyāsi:
‘ime dhammā virāgāya saṃvattanti, no sarāgāya; visaṃyogāya saṃvattanti, no saṃyogāya;
en: But, Gotamī, those things of which you might know:
‘These things lead (1) to the fading away of craving,
not to craving; (2) to non-attachment, not to bondage;
(3) to discarding, not to accumulating;
(4) to fewness of desires, not to many desires;
(5) to contentment, not to lack of contentment;
(6) to solitude, not to socializing;
(7) to the arousing of energy, not to laziness;
(8) to being easy to support, not to being difficult to support,’

pali: ‘eso dhammo, eso vinayo, etaṃ satthu sāsanan’”ti.
en: you should bear in mind, Gotamī, certainly:
‘This is the Dhamma; this is the discipline;
this is the teaching of the Teacher.’”
“Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus: ‘Now I address you, bhikkhus:
conditioned things are of the nature to vanish;
strive without heedlessness to attain [the goal].’
This was the last statement of the Tathāgata.”
The bhikkhu who abides in mettā,
and has confidence in the teachings of the Buddha,
would attain the peaceful state,
the happiness of the stilling of conditioned things.
It is not by hatred
that hatred is ever settled in this world.
By kindness hatred is settled.
This is an eternal law.
So very happily we live,
kind among the hostile;
among hostile people,
we live kindly.

“Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘We will develop and cultivate the liberation of mind by mettā, make it our vehicle, make it our basis, stabilize it, exercise ourselves in it, and fully undertake it.’
Thus should you train yourselves.”

suttas.title: mettāsahagatena cetasā
suttas.en: With a Mind Suffused with mettā

pali: ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatha; tathā dutiyaṃ, tathā tatiyaṃ, tathā catutthaṃ. iti uddham, adho, tiriyaṃ, sabbadhi,
en: “Come, bhikkhus, dwell pervading one quarter with a mind suffused with mettā, likewise the second quarter, the third quarter, and the fourth quarter.
Thus above, below, across, and everywhere,
and to all as to oneself, dwell pervading the entire world with a mind suffused with mettā, vast, exalted, boundless, without hostility, without ill-will.”

pali: “mettāya, bhikkhave, ceto-vimuttiyā āsevitāya, bhāvitāya, bahulī-katāya, yānī-katāya, vatthu-katāya, anuṭṭhitāya, paricitāya, susamāraddhāya ekādas’ānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā. katame ekādasa?
en: “Bhikkhus, when the liberation of the mind by mettā has been pursued, developed, and cultivated, made a vehicle and basis, carried out, consolidated, and properly undertaken, eleven benefits are to be expected. What eleven?

pali: sukhaṃ supati, sukhaṃ paṭibujjhati, na pāpakaṃ supinaṃ passati, manussānaṃ piyo hoti, amanussānaṃ piyo hoti, devatā rakkhanti, n’āssa aggi vā visaṃ vā satthaṃ vā kamati, tuvaṭaṃ cittaṃ samādhiyati, mukha-vaṇṇo vippasīdati, asammūḷho kālaṃ karoti, uttariṃ appaṭivijjhanto brahma-lok’ūpago hoti.
en: (1) One sleeps well; (2) one awakens happily; (3) one does not have bad dreams; (4) one is pleasing to human beings; (5) one is pleasing to spirits; (6) deities protect one; (7) fire, poison, and weapons do not injure one; (8) one’s mind quickly becomes concentrated; (9) one’s facial complexion is serene; (10) one dies unconfused; and (11) if one does not penetrate further, one fares on to the brahmā world.

pali: mettāya, bhikkhave, ceto-vimuttiyā āsevitāya, bhāvitāya, bahulī-katāya, yānī-katāya, vatthu-katāya, anuṭṭhitāya, paricitāya, susamāraddhāya ime ekādas’ānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
en: When, bhikkhus, the liberation of the mind by mettā has been repeatedly pursued, developed, and cultivated, made a vehicle and basis, carried out, consolidated, and properly undertaken, these eleven benefits are to be expected.”

pali: “… te’pi kho āyasmanto bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekam antaṃ nisīdiṃsu. ekam antaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ anuruddhaṃ bhagavā etad avoca:
en: “… Then those three venerable ones paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side.
When they were seated, the Blessed One said to them:

pali: na ca mayaṃ, bhante, piṇḍakena kilamāmā”ti.
en: “I hope you are all keeping well, Anuruddha,
I hope you are all comfortable,
I hope you are not having any trouble getting almsfood.”
“We are keeping well, Blessed One, we are comfortable, and we are not having any trouble getting almsfood.”

pali: “kacci pana vo, anuruddhā, samaggā, sammodamānā, avivadamānā, khīr’odakī-bhūtā,
“taggha mayaṃ, bhante, samaggā, sammodamānā, avivadamānā, khīr’odakī-bhūtā,
en: “I hope, Anuruddha, that you are all living in harmony, with mutual appreciation, without disputing, blending like milk and water, viewing each other with kindly eyes.”
“Surely, venerable sir, we are living in harmony,
with mutual appreciation, without disputing, blending like milk and water, viewing each other with kindly eyes.”

pali: “yathā kathaṃ pana tumhe, anuruddhā, samaggā, sammodamānā, avivadamānā, khīr’odakī-bhūtā,
“idha mayhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ hoti: ‘lābhā vata me, suladdhaṃ vata me, yo’haṃ eva’rūpehi sabrahma-cārīhi saddhiṃ viharāmī’ti.
mettaṃ kāya-kammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi c’eva raho ca;
mettaṃ vacī-kammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi c’eva raho ca;
mettaṃ mano-kammaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ āvi c’eva raho ca.
en: “But, Anuruddha, how do you live thus?”
“Venerable sir, as to that, I think thus: ‘It is a gain for me, it is a great gain for me, that I am living with such companions in the spiritual life.’
I maintain bodily acts of mettā towards those
venerable ones both openly and privately;
I maintain verbal acts of mettā towards them
both openly and privately;
I maintain mental acts of mettā towards them both openly and privately.

pali: so kho ahaṃ, bhante, sakaṃ cittaṃ nikkhipitvā,
nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā, ekañ ca pana maññe cittan”ti.
en: I consider: ‘Why should I not set aside what I wish to do and go along with what these venerable ones wish to do?’
Then I set aside what I wish to do and go along with what these venerable ones wish to do.
We are different in body, venerable sir,
but as if one in mind.”

pali: nānā hi kho no, bhante, kāyā, ekañ ca pana maññe cittan”ti.
en: The venerable Nandiya and the venerable Kimbila each spoke likewise, [adding]:

pali: “evaṃ kho mayaṃ, bhante, samaggā, sammodamānā, avivadamānā, khīr’odakī-bhūtā,
en: “That is how, venerable sir, we are living in harmony,
with mutual appreciation, without disputing, blending like milk and water, viewing each other with kindly eyes.”
“Good, good, Anuruddha!”

pali: tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṃ aññataro bhikkhu
en: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
Now on that occasion, in Sāvatthī, a certain bhikkhu had been bitten by a snake and had died.

pali: atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā ten’upasaṅkamiṃsu;
ekam antaṃ nisīdiṃsu. ekam antaṃ nisinnā kho,
te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etad avocuṃ: “idha, bhante, sāvatthiyaṃ aññataro bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṅ-kato”ti.
en: Then a number of bhikkhus approached the
Blessed One, paid homage to him,
sat down to one side, and said:
“Venerable sir, a certain bhikkhu here in Sāvatthī was bitten by a snake and died.”

pali: “na ha nūna so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cattāri ahi-rāja-kulāni mettena cittena phari. sace hi so, bhikkhave,
bhikkhu cattāri ahi-rāja-kulāni mettena cittena phareyya,
na hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṅ-kareyya.
en: [The Buddha:] “Surely, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu did not pervade the four royal families of snakes with a mind of mettā. For if he had done so,
he would not have been bitten by a snake and died.

pali: na ha nūna so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahi-rāja-kulāni mettena cittena phari. sace hi so, bhikkhave,
bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahi-rāja-kulāni mettena cittena phareyya,
na hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṅ-kareyya.
en: What are the four? The virūpakkha royal family of snakes, the erāpatha royal family of snakes,
the chabyāputta royal family of snakes,
and the black gotamaka royal family of snakes. Surely, that bhikkhu did not pervade these four royal families of snakes with a mind of mettā.
For if he had done so, he would not have been bitten by a snake and died.

pali: anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imāni cattāri ahi-rāja-kulāni mettena cittena pharituṃ; atta-guttiyā, atta-rakkhāya, atta-parittāyā”ti.
en: I enjoin you, bhikkhus, to pervade these four royal families of snakes with a mind of mettā,
for your own security, safety, and protection.
I have mettā for the virūpakkha snakes;
for the erāpatha snakes I have mettā.
I have mettā for the chabyāputta snakes;
for the black gotamakas I have mettā.
I have mettā for footless creatures;
for those with two feet I have mettā.
I have mettā for those with four feet;
for those with many feet I have mettā.
May footless beings not harm me;
may no harm come to me from those with two feet;
may four-footed beings not harm me;
may no harm come to me from those with many feet.
May all beings, all living things,
all creatures, every one,
meet with good fortune;
may nothing bad come to anyone.
The Buddha is measureless,
the Dhamma is measureless,
the Saṅgha is measureless;
creeping things, snakes, scorpions, centipedes, spiders, lizards, and rats are finite.

pali: katā me rakkhā, katā me parittā,
en: I have made a safeguard, I have made protection.
Let the creatures retreat.
I pay homage to the Blessed One,
homage to the seven Perfectly Enlightened Ones.”

pali: “yaṃ kiñci vittaṃ idha vā huraṃ vā,
en: “Whatever treasure exists here or beyond,
or the sublime gem in the heavens,
there is none equal to the Tathāgata.
This too is the sublime gem in the Buddha:
by this truth, may there be well-being!
The excellent one, knower of the excellent,
giver of the excellent, bringer of the excellent,
the unsurpassed one taught the excellent Dhamma.
This too is the sublime gem in the Buddha:
by this truth, may there be well-being!
Whatever beings are gathered here,
whether of the earth, or in the sky,
we pay homage to the thus-gone Buddha,
venerated by devas and humans; may there be well-being!
Whatever beings are gathered here,
whether of the earth, or in the sky,
we pay homage to the thus-gone Dhamma,
venerated by devas and humans; may there be well-being!
Whatever beings are gathered here,
whether of the earth, or in the sky,
we pay homage to the thus-gone Saṅgha,
venerated by devas and humans; may there be well-being!”
May I be free of hatred;
may I be free of ill-will;
may I be free of misery;
may I keep myself happy.
May my mother, my father, my teachers,
my relatives, and everyone
be free of hatred;
be free of ill-will;
be free of misery;
may they keep themselves happy.
May all beings, all living beings,
all creatures, all individuals,
all beings possessed of a sense of individuality,
all women, all men,
all noble ones, all non-noble ones,
all devas, all human beings,
all those fallen into the lower realms,
be free of hatred;
be free of ill-will;
be free of misery;
may they keep themselves happy.
“May all beings be happy and secure;
may they be inwardly happy!
Whatever living beings there are
whether frail or firm, without omission,
those that are long or those that are large,
middling, short, tiny or massive;
whether they are seen or unseen,
whether they dwell far or near,
whether they have come to be or will come to be,
may all beings be inwardly happy!”
I have no other refuge,
the Buddha is my supreme refuge;
by this proclamation of truth,
may you gain victory and happiness.
I have no other refuge,
the Dhamma is my supreme refuge;
by this proclamation of truth,
may victory and happiness be yours.
I have no other refuge,
the Saṅgha is my supreme refuge;
by this proclamation of truth,
may all beings be happy.
